neighborhood_overview: Portobello is an exceptional place to live - very sought after - right by the leafy Grand Canal with its walk ways and cycle track, where you can also go kayaking or simply admire the swans. It's within walking distance of all visitor attractions - or on a bus route to the more remote ones. It feels like real 'old' Dublin and is full of eateries and bars and venues - it really is the most desirable of locations in the entire city. The area has a very youthful feel to it and is full of life and energy. Portobello is an area stretching westwards from South Richmond Street as far as Upper Clanbrassil Street bordered on the north by the South Circular Road and on the south by the Grand Canal. As a fast-expanding Dublin suburb during the 19th century, Portobello attracted many upwardly-mobile families whose members went on to play important roles in politics, the arts and the sciences.

name: Unique Central Dublin River-view
summary: My apartment provides an immaculate, comfortable, safe and quiet space right in the very heart of Dublin's city centre. I am a highly experienced host, with multiple 5 star reviews and a 100% response record. I'm told that my apartment is a real reflection of my involvement in the creative arts and is totally unique. This is not an anonymous, corporate sterile environment, but neither is it a typical family style home filled with "wooly" goods!
space: My apartment overlooks the River Liffey with its famous Halfpenny Bridge in the Temple Bar area of Dublin. You literally can walk around the corner, from my fantastic riverside location, to enjoy your time in Ireland's capital, or you can use my apartment as a base from which to enjoy the rest of the country.  Many have remarked on the great view from my front windows. A recent visitor made this expression on arrival: "wow - this is actually even nicer than the photographs show". You can chill out at my kitchen table, (which is the size of two touching dinner plates), as you watch the river ebbing and flowing, and the non-stop stream of pedestrians on the new foot bridge.  There is quick, easy access (3 mins walk) to the Luas tram which connects the two main railway stations and central bus terminal Busarus. Please try resist any urges to re-arrange the furniture, or play games of musical chairs with my two kitchen seats :-) Generally, just treat my home with care and respect. Please try to schedule your arrival for BEFORE 9.30pm. Bring a sense of humour and good spirit.  Be organised. Be prepared to have a wonderful time.
host_about:
I am a visual artist and part-time lecturer at a college in Ireland.  My friends have said that the second image of me with cat friend timelessly reveals my personality well, which is obviously too nice to ignore :-) (even though it was taken about ten years ago!)

I'm a total animal lover - especially cats, though I don't have one in Dublin.

I am an experienced traveller/host/home exchanger, and enjoy having visitors in my apartment during the times when I am not there. I like meeting people, and love my job as an art college lecturer.

I am careful and selective about my guests, as this is my home, and I try to keep it in immaculate order. I prefer personal contact and establishing a trusting, friendly relationship with those who stay. I particularly welcome guests from the creative community. ie fellow artists/designers/writers/dancers/photographers/actors.

Over time, several guests have returned, and others have become personal friends.

I am also a committed environmentalist and vegetarian, so expect lots of recommendations for good food restaurants! I place great value on humour, creativity, stamina, trust, respect and being resourceful. 

Every day I wait for news about my grant application for starting a course, to teach the River Liffey seagulls how to perform replicas of Busby Berkeley routines to entertain the tourists on the boardwalks.

neighborhood_overview: A beautiful, historic residential square, built in 1790's, within 5-10 minutes walk of down-town city centre. Elegance and convenience combined with a bit of inner city grittiness. I have loved it all, since 1978! Mountjoy Square is situated just NE of the historic city centre, within walking distance of just about all the main city attractions. It is the most densely populated area in the entire city: 1500 people have front doors opening onto the Square. The house fronts onto a 4acre/1.5ha park, across a fairly busy street. This apartment faces the side street, so it is quieter, but you will still hear traffic.....Please bear in mind that this is NOT LEAFY SUBURBIA, but a vibrant, living city community and it's definitely gritty in places... Having said that, I have lived here, uneventfully, for nearly 38 years, and consider the trade-offs well worth it, for the excitement and convenience of having the city on my doorstep..

neighborhood_overview: Location cannot be better. You are overlooking the River Liffey and directly above the beautiful Ha'penny Bridge. Cross the bridge and you are in Temple Bar with its numerous bars, restaurants, vintage clothes shops, Project Arts Centre, Gallery of Photography, Irish Film Institute and many other attractions.  Dublin two main pedestrian shopping streets, Grafton and Henry St are about 5 minutes away.  Trinity College with its famous Library is 3 minutes walk.  Dublin is experiencing a Renaissance after a long recession and every week a new exciting restaurant, cultural space or play is opening. It is a great time to be visiting!
notes: Please also consider that this apartment is right in the very heart of Dublin City. host_about:
I am a dentist working in Trinity College Dublin, Ireland. I am English and moved to this wonderful city 7 years ago so I know it pretty well by now. I also have a home in Turkey and travel there as often as I can to pick up some sun....although the weather in ireland is better than its reputation suggests and I have very many sunny mornings drinking coffee on my balcony with great views as far as the Wicklow Mountains and the Dublin coastline
I love to travel and when I am visiting somewhere - I prefer to spend time getting to really know somewhere rather than passing though it, and Dublin certainly deserves more than a passing visit and has a lot more to offer than Temple Bar and the Guiness Factory!
I speak Spanish fluently, have a smattering of french, german and turkish - but I can usually find a way to communicate and connect with people wherever I am in the world.  I enjoy live music, theatre and film. I am happy wandering or traveling alone - but also love to spend time with my dear friends and meeting new people.
I can't live without good coffee, an internet connection, my dearest friends and family ...... and the freedom to travel and get away from all of the above from time to time ;)
I enjoy traveling including planning trips as often as possible - but once I am away I try to be spontaneous and flexible and take things as they come.....whats's it like to have me as a guest........well hassle free I hope;)
....what's it like to stay at my place - well I would say its relaxed and easy going, with as much or as little conversation and privacy as you choose....

neighborhood_overview: Just North of the River Liffey and a short walk from historic O'Connell Street, this is the very heart of the city centre and the perfect location for anyone wishing to explore the city by foot. One of Dublin’s main shopping hubs is O'Connell Street (and its tributary, the ever-busy Henry Street), which culminates in a spearhead of excellent museums dotted around Parnell Square (most notably the Hugh Lane Gallery). To the west of here is the up-and-coming Smithfield and, further still, the vast Phoenix Park (also home to Dublin Zoo) while just across the bridge to the south is the formidable campus of Trinity College, with its ancient claim to fame in pride of place in the Old Library & Book of Kells. You have everything at your doorstep in the city centre and there's an exciting mix of cultures and ideas to cater for every whim you might have.  Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!
notes: There is on-street parking anywhere around the square outside the house. 24 hour parking discs can be provided with the property.
transit: Getting to and from the Airport couldn’t be easier. The 747 Airlink Express Bus runs direct from the Dublins central bus station (BusAras) which is just a short walk from the apartment, and costs €10 return. Alternatively, you can take a 20-30 minutes taxi that will cost roughly €20-€30, depending on traffic. If arriving by train, the apartment is located close to Connolly Station, so you will not be far from your front door! The DART and LUAS (Dublin's light rail systems) also stop at Connolly station, and it is a short 15 minute train to Dublin's beaches and beautiful cliff walks.  Being so central, most of your journeys can be made by foot. If you would prefer using public transport, you will also have easy access to several bus routes on O’Connell street. Pick up a Leap card from a local newsagent or Connolly Station and you will be able to use all public transport across the city while you are here. host_about:
I am a dentist working in Trinity College Dublin, Ireland. I am English and moved to this wonderful city 7 years ago so I know it pretty well by now. I also have a home in Turkey and travel there as often as I can to pick up some sun....although the weather in ireland is better than its reputation suggests and I have very many sunny mornings drinking coffee on my balcony with great views as far as the Wicklow Mountains and the Dublin coastline
I love to travel and when I am visiting somewhere - I prefer to spend time getting to really know somewhere rather than passing though it, and Dublin certainly deserves more than a passing visit and has a lot more to offer than Temple Bar and the Guiness Factory!
I speak Spanish fluently, have a smattering of french, german and turkish - but I can usually find a way to communicate and connect with people wherever I am in the world.  I enjoy live music, theatre and film. I am happy wandering or traveling alone - but also love to spend time with my dear friends and meeting new people.
I can't live without good coffee, an internet connection, my dearest friends and family ...... and the freedom to travel and get away from all of the above from time to time ;)
I enjoy traveling including planning trips as often as possible - but once I am away I try to be spontaneous and flexible and take things as they come.....whats's it like to have me as a guest........well hassle free I hope;)
....what's it like to stay at my place - well I would say its relaxed and easy going, with as much or as little conversation and privacy as you choose....

space: This is a large two bed apartment, bigger than my penthouse in the same building. It is newly converted from an architects office and retains the beautiful features of high ceilings, large sash windows and paneled doors. Adelaide road is a tree lined avenue and is around the corner from two Hilton hotels. The Grand canal is around the corner and has a great cycling and walking track. The restaurants and nightlife of Harcourt St and Camden St are a short walk away.

host_about:
I am from Dublin, Ireland but have spent quite a bit of time in Kansas, USA, and have travelled extensively since I was a teenager. As an experienced traveller I know what it is that is most precious to those who find themselves in foreign cultures; a clean bed, a welcoming host, some insights into where the locals go to eat and drink. I have taken all these thoughts and combined them into an experience that I love to have in my own travels. 

I am a founder member of the Dublin Host Ambassador Group for Airbnb. Our group advises them of improvements we feel will enhance the whole Airbnb experience and we also direct new hosts on the road to creating positive memorable guest interactions.

While I am always pleased to meet people from any corner of the world, I have to admit that I have an immense fondness for Americans, this comes out of great experience I had living there when I was younger and for the huge amount of support and encouragement I received from some many Americans over so many years. I have not yet an American that I did not like!

I have also made many visits to Germany, Austria and Switzerland and enjoy interacting with guests from that neck of the woods. Please bear in mind though, that my German speaking skills extend to being able to order a beer and a donut :-)

I am a photographer who runs his own photography school which allows me to travel around Ireland, Europe and the USA to shoot scenes that I like, many of these are on the walls of the apartment. If you are also a keen photographer then I look forward to talking cameras, techniques and creativity with you. If you are not then I still look forward to hearing your story!

Alice Coghlan is a theatre and opera director with Irish/English/American heritage who runs her own company in Dublin Wonderland Productions - wonderlandtheatre, whose work includes literary audio walks of James Joyce's Dublin, children's theatre workshops and dinner theatre. She is also a qualified cook and loves to experiment with all the foods of the world and cook for our guests! 

In our spare time we love all things cultural and are very involved in the Dublin arts world and actually met by chance in a Dublin art gallery. We also enjoy hillwalking, movies, fine living, fun times and above all travel!

We may also be able to offer you individual pottery or cookery classes with us during your stay, and you're also very welcome to visit Radek's pottery and to learn how pottery is made. 

We love being guests and hosts Airbnb so much that the the Irish Media got in contact with us, and one interview has led to another and we've been having a great time. Look us up 'listen again links' on radio shows RTE 1 Morning Ireland, Today FM Business Show on a Sunday or in newspapers Irish Independent and Daily Mail. It's called The Dropping Well- it's a real Irish "local" and is very popular.  Some people argue it has the best Guinness in Dublin!   -- There are lots more pubs, restaurants and shops within a short walk or tram ride of the house.  Ranelagh village is only a few minutes away and is very popular amongst us locals for its fantastic pub and restaurant scene.  Dundrum Town Centre is a few minutes the other direction and has a huge shopping centre and lots of excellent restaurants.   -- The city centre is within very easy reach, exactly 10 mins by Luas [tram], and my house is also very convenient for getting to places such as UCD, Trinity College, the RD
notes: I'm happy to facilitate early morning check ins- I know what it's like to arrive early into a new town!  :-)  Late arrivals are also welcome.
transit: Milltown Luas [tram] stop is right at the end of our driveway- it couldn't be more convenient!  It's exactly 10 minutes to the city centre, and the  villages of Ranelagh and Dundrum are even closer on the same line.  As you can imagine, my car doesn't get much use! --  It's easy to get to my home from the airport, ports and train stations using public transport.  Full details are provided with your reservation.  If you are driving, I will be happy to provide directions from wherever you are coming from.
access: My guests are welcome to relax and enjoy the house.  The kitchen is available to make light snacks, but not for cooking.
interaction: I am very happy to help with suggestions for my guests' visit.  I love meeting people and helping them to have a more authentic experience of my city!  Dublin is a great place to live, having all the benefits of a big city while retaining its local charm and friendliness.  I am delighted to share a local's perspective on where to go and what to do.   When I'm home, I'm there if you need me and I'm happy to chat, but I give guests their own space too.
house_rules: **When sending a booking/request, please introduce yourself with your full name and the names of any other guests who will be coming, so that I know who will be staying with me in my home!  :-) - I hope my guests enjoy their visit, and I just ask that they be respectful and treat my home with care, leaving everything as they find it.   - I have no difficulty with guests going out and enjoying Dublin's vibrant social scene during their visit (in fact, I encourage it!).  However, it is important that guests are quiet and not disruptive to me or my neighbours if they arrive home late.   - For security reasons, all external doors and windows must be locked before leaving the house. - Please note cooking facilities are not available to guests.  However, a light breakfast is provided and guests are welcome to use the kitchen to make tea/coffee and snacks as they like. - Strictly no smoking in or around the house (including in the garden- the smell comes back inside with the smoker!).  Thanks
host_about:
I am a professional in my 30s and come from Dublin originally.  I love travelling and have been lucky enough to see a lot of the world [but there's many more places on my list!].  

Other than travel, I am a big rugby fan and hold a season ticket for my local team, Leinster (who play within walking distance of my home), and I love doing Pilates and yoga.  I also enjoy watching NFL, thanks to my time living in the US!

  When not enjoying all the numerous delights that the city has to offer, you will find me walking along the coast road, which has been compared to The Amalfi Coast of Italy, past lots of famous homes to the heritage village of Dalkey, with its quaint shops, pubs and restaurants. When not out walking, I travel on the little electric train, known as "The Dart" into the city or out along the coast.

When I travel to other parts of the world, I prefer to stay in Airbnb places rather than hotels  when I can!

Within 10 minutes of the house I am in the large gardens and fields of the Victorian Herbert Park, or in the leafy walks of Merrion Square, or enjoying the stunning views of Dublin from the rooftop bar of the Marker Hotel. l can cross the road to take the Dodder River walk to the Grand Canal Dock and over to the River Liffey. The Lansdowne Road/Aviva Stadium is two minutes walk from the house, the RDS is six minutes walk, the Bord Gais/Grand Canal and LIR Theatres are six/seven minutes walk . The O2 is twenty minutes walk.  The village of Ballsbridge  and the RDS is five minutes walk away and has numerous restaurants and pubs. Beggars Bush is four minutes in the opposite direction and again has award-winning restaurants, famous pubs and a supermarket open 24/7. The Grand Canal Dock is seven minutes walk away. notes: The local village of Beggars Bush is 2/3 minutes walk from the house at the crossroads of Shelbourne Road, Bath Ave, South Lotts Road and Haddington Road- you'll find a 24-hour Eurospar shop there, a pharmacy the superb South Lotts Grocery store and Deli - don't miss going there and you'll also find the famous Slatterys pub. In terms of restaurants you'll find Juniors, Paulie's pizza and Foodgame (don't miss their lunches) which all have websites that are worth checking out and Farmer Browns is excellent for brunch and for afternoon teas with home baking.  All these are eateries very close by and are excellent in terms of quality and price. There are also two gastro pubs - The Old Spot is superb and has a great range of boutique Irish Gins and the other is called the Chop House which is good but in my opinion is not as good as all the other restaurants- but they specialise in steaks so if you crave a grass-fed Irish cut of meat - don't miss it.  The best chipper in Dublin is the Italia

host_about: I'm a Dubliner who loves beautiful places, spaces, music, history, art and food. I adore local places with long histories and like to get to know them. My desert island foods would be crumbly blue cheese on an oat biscuit, butter and whiskey wrapped fresh lobster and Cork dry gin with slices of homegrown cucumber and ice. I can't live without good coffee and wouldn't even try. I'm currently reading Hal Fisher's A History of Europe and I love the knowledge it shares about Western Europe since 1731. Right now I'm catching up on my local history over the last 100 years...bound to happen in 2016 ... as the 100 years since the rising that sparked Ireland's independence comes calling.   My favourite musicians are plenty - Queen,  The Mumfords, Daft Punk and closer to home U2 and Mark Geary. I believe in keeping life simple - and I fundamentally believe - the simpler, the better. I enjoy welcoming guests to Dublin and sharing stories of local history, culture and food.

summary: This property is located over a horse stable that is occasionally used by the Mounted Unit of An Garda Siochana.  It is quiet spacious; and the big surprise is the peace and quiet even though it's in the heart of Dublin city.
space: History The mews building at the rear of No.63 Merrion Square is an integral part of one of the most significant survivals of an 18th century Dublin townhouse  - comprising main house with garden, mews and stables with its own small garden - within the classic Fitzwilliam/Merrion Square area of Dublin. Situated on Fizwilliam Lane the Mews is a quaint and charming property. Built in 1792/93 the house retains much of its historic character and fabric. The Mews also has a private garden, coach yard coach house and stables. The stables have been conserved, and given a new life as a place to rest and water the horses of the Mounted Unit of An Garda Siochana while they are on duty in the city centre. neighborhood_overview: A truly wonderful location in a quiet, leafy little street, close to all the main attractions Dublin has to offer. Great pubs and restaurants in Ballsbridge or in the pretty village of Sandymount are both just a short five minute stroll away, with a Tesco supermarket, a good butcher, greengrocers (which also sells some speciality health foods), a book shop, some nice boutiques and some very good restaurants and famous pubs. There are also landmark pubs, excellent restaurants in Ballsbridge which is even closer but has less of a 'village' atmosphere. Our favourite thing is to walk to the Poolbeg light house for sweeping views of Dublin Bay - and if you're lucky you will find a fisherman selling mackerel straight out of the sea!
notes: Extremely close to the RDS where the legendary Dublin Horse Show is held each August.  In summer, you can have a barbecue in the garden or take a stroll down to Sandymount beach. You can meet all your grocery shopping requirements at the Tesco in Sandymount.

host_about:
Hi we're Nicola and Eamon. 
This is our spacious family home in the quiet but very centrally located Ballsbridge area. The Intercontinental hotel is just close by so it's a great neighbourhood.
The famous Irish poet WB Yeats was born around the corner on Sandymount avenue! 
The Dart (light rail) is literally a two minute walk from the house. It brings you right into the city in ten minutes - or out to the pretty seaside towns and villages of Howth, Dalkey and Killiney where you can stroll around the shops and sample the local seafood.
The house was built in 1892 - it's on a lovely terrace overlooking a little park and tennis court owned by the residents of our street. 
You can catch a glimpse of the famous rugby venue, the Aviva stadium right at the top of the road.
The RDS - home to the legendary Dublin Horse Show is less than five minute's walk away.
The picturesque village of Sandymount is also very close by - with nice little shops, cafes and lovely restaurants for a very easy and relaxed night out.
We renovated the house top to bottom recently but did our best to maintain the character and charm. 
It's a lovely warm family home, 140 sq metres large. It has a great kitchen with a 'snug' just off it where you can watch tv in front of an antique French stove in which we burn wood and Irish turf.
A tranquil sitting room at the front overlooks the park and it has an open fire where you can sit and read peacefully, listening to the radio, relaxing after a day of sightseeing!
A little bit about us: We are college buddies who first met while studying in University in Galway, now we're married with 3 kids. 
Pre-kids we did a good bit of travelling but post-kids we've done even more! Among our favourite places on the planet are Buenos Aires, Budapest and Kyoto. We consider ourselves easy going and fun and would love people to enjoy our home in our absence!
We are very proud of our Airbnb 'superhost' status - thanks to all the lovely guests we've hosted so far - and we work hard to maintain it!!

neighborhood_overview: Adamstown is a great neighbourhood. It is close enough to Dublin that you can get in to the city in less than 20 minutes by train, but it is nice to get a little taste of life in Dublin outside of the city too. I live close to Lucan village which is a typical small Irish village. You can find many pubs (one that has a traditional thatched roof!) and restaurants in the village, even though it is quite small. It is such a nice village that the Italian ambassador decided to call it home!  One of the best secrets about Adamstown is that just behind the house, hiding behind some trees is a very old country house hotel! Finnstown house is our neighbor, there you will feel like you have taken a walk back in time to a much older Ireland in this authentic old Irish country house. You can have a meal, or just a drink here or even take a peaceful walk around the grounds, where you will meet the resident...llamas and an ostrich!!! Only in Dublin! ;)
notes: We are a dog household so you would need to like dogs to stay here :)
transit: For your convenience, we have our very own train station, Adamstown Station! This brings you directly into Heuston Station in Dublin City! Take this short train ride and you will find yourself on the river liffey, beside the Guinness factory and Phoenix park! Trains run once an hour. It's best to get the visitor leap card to get the best price. You can buy this in Dublin airport in the shops in both Terminal 1 & 2. These cards are great and can be used on all trains, trams and buses in and around Dublin! You also have the option to take a bus in to the city, it takes a little longer (the bus likes to stop everywhere!) ;) but they go every 15 minutes. There is also a nightlink bus that takes you from the city back home on Friday and Saturday nights. It runs at midnight, 1am, 2am, 3am and 4am and costs only €6.60!
access: In addition to your own double bedroom and private bathroom, you also have full access to the kitchen at any time of the day or night. It has a fridge/freezer, cooker, microwave and a dishwasher. Feel free to help yourself to any food in the house and also to stock up the kitchen with anything you buy.  You also have full access to the sitting room where you can relax after a long day of sightseeing, watch a movie (there is a big selection!) or play the piano. You will also have your own key to the house so you can come and go as you please :)

neighborhood_overview: Adjacent to the apartment is Dublin Castle, the seat of British power in Ireland for almost 700 years. You are also located within minutes of other cultural attractions including: - the Chester Beatty Library, one of the best museums in Europe - the magnificent St. Patrick’s Cathedral that houses Jonathan Swift's remains (he wrote Gulliver's Travels)  - Christ Church Cathedral,one of Dublin's oldest buildings and a place of pilgrimage for almost 1,000 years.  - Trinity College, where you can see the famous Book of Kells The Guinness Storehouse, home to the black stuff and an important part of Ireland’s history, is a 15 minute walk, and nearby Kilmainham Jail was notorious in the 19th century for its harsh treatment of prisoners.  The apartment is also located beside Dublinia which is a self-guided walk that helps you explore Dublin City in more detail. Other ways of learning about the city include the Open Top Buses, Walking Tours, Cycling Tours for the more energetic, Literary Tours,
notes: If you are arriving by car, on street parking is available free from 7pm to 7am on Monday to Saturday and free all day Sunday. At other times the cost is 2.90 euro per hour. Alternatively you can park in one of the nearby city centre carparks. Typical cost is 18euro per 24 hours. Some car parks provide a 2 day or 5 day option. Christchurch Parking ( (Website hidden by Airbnb) website) across the road from the apartment provide overnight parking for €10 from 6pm to 9am. Opening hours are 7am (10am Sundays and bank holidays) to midnight. They also offer a 5 day parking rate. You could also check Fleet st Parking, Drury St parking or Stephens Green parking (all 10 mins walk).

The red line provides access to the city's 2 main railway stations - Heuston and Connolly, and to the main intercity bus station, Busarus.

neighborhood_overview: The house is situated at the edge of the bohemian Camden Street, Wexford Street and Portobello area but is also considered as 'South City Centre' where most of the Dublin nightlife is. Synge Street is less than 10 minutes walking distance from Dublin's main shopping and restaurant district and cultural quarter surrounding Grafton Street. Our neighbourhood is very central but offers a vibrant alternative to the regular Dublin tourist traps even though Temple Bar is a mere 15 minute walk away.
notes: Mi casa es su casa! Please make yourself at home! • It is advisable to book one night before your arrival if you require an early morning check-in to ensure early access. • The south inner city is the true city centre where all the best shopping, cultural activity and nightlife is. Visitors are often disappointed when they stay in the north inner city and discover the O'Connell street area is NOT the the main focus of Dublin urban activity and has very little street life at night. • See my guide book/map for a sample of my recommendations. • Why not stay longer and use the house as a base for your complete Irish visit? Make sure not to leave anything on view inside your car.
transit: Dublin is a walking city and this house is very centrally located, but we are also 3 minutes away from bus stops bringing you directly to the airport and other city areas. The Luas tram service is also nearby and 'Dublinbikes' are available to rent right around the corner 24/7. Taxis are plentiful and Dublin uses the 'HAILO' app which you can download to your phone for free.
access: This is a 2 story house with steps up to the hall door. You will have sole access to the house including bedrooms, bathroom, toilet, kitchen, living room and back garden. I work in the hospitality and entertainment industry and have a good insight into some of Dublin's best kept secrets.
interaction: I will meet you on arrival to hand over keys, then the house is entirely yours! neighborhood_overview: Our house was built by the Iveagh Trust  (originally the Guinness Trust) between 1926 and 1936 on 30 acres of land just off the the Crumlin Road. The Iveagh Trust was set up by Edward Cecil Guinness the first Earl of Iveagh in 1890 to provide excellent housing for the labouring classes in Dublin. Our house is one of 137 special properties provided to the workers from the St. James' street brewery where Guinness was first brewed 255 years ago. Although most of the house's in the estate are no longer owned by Guinness workers the "Black Stuff" is still brewed at St James's gate to this day and many of the houses still pay land rent to the Iveagh Trust.

 Jane x

The rejuvenated Dublin docklands is now home to the european headquarters of the worlds 2 largest search engine corps, social media corps and Airbnb to mention but a few, making the Boathouse an ideal place to stay for business or pleasure. Its a pleasant 10 min walk through the park to the village and then on towards the city centre, by bus or by Luas (tram) for ten minutes more. We're within walking distance of the Bord Gais Theatre offering a selection of Westend and broadway touring shows. It was designed by architect Daniel Libeskind in the beautiful settings of the Grand Canal Harbour; 20mins walk. The harbour area has a variety of restaurants and places to sit out while enjoying a coffee or a glass of wine and is always a great place to go on a warm evening. The Dart line (Light rail along the coast to Howth harbour or Greystones, Co. Wicklow) is a 20 min walk. A 12min walk just over the bridge in Ringsend Village there a Dublin-Bike scheme depot, (3day pass €5, rent free for first 30mins, small charge thereafter). You just use em for twenty mins and leave it at another depot, then pick up another for you next trip!

interaction: We offer a relaxed warm welcome to guests and are happy to share our knowledge of Dublin and the many attractions here. I love living in  Dublin and am sometimes accused of being a little fanatical about it, but its just a fantastic city. Some of my favourites pastimes are walking the dog (Ally our golden retriever) along the pier to Poolbeg lighthouse, strolling through Temple bar, drinking a Guinness with friends and enjoying the craic (that's not cocaine, just Irish for having a laugh), Taking a coffee in Bewleys and a stroll on Grafton St. or just a visit to the old library in Trinity College and wander through front square to soak up the atmosphere to mention but a few. I love hillwalking in Wicklow, motor cruising on the Shannon, photography, cinema and theatre going. If you like any of these things I will be happy to try to guide you towards the best of them.
house_rules: Just a few things to note...  We ask that guests do not smoke indoors, but you are welcome to smoke outside - we even have a smoking seat in the garden! The ground floor is finished in tile and hardwood so downstairs you are welcome to wear what ever foot wear you feel comfortable in.:-) In the breakfast room we provide everything that you will need in order to prepare your own breakfast, fridge, kettle, tea and coffee, toaster, microwave, cutlery and delph. If guests wish to use this area in the evenings to enjoy a light snack or order in a meal, they are most welcome to do so. However we kindly ask that guests do not bring food or drinks up to their bedroom.  The host's kitchen is private.
host_about:
I love travel and have tried to take a significant trip between each career move. My favourite places so far include Guatemala, the Caya's off Belize, Sitges in Spain, the foothills of the Himalayas in northern India and more recently San Francisco. 
I love cooking and gardening and grow some of our own vegetables, which I am delighted to be able to do in the middle of the city.  We keep some chickens in a dome shaped house called an Eggloo, made by an insensitively named company called Omlet co
Ally, our golden retriever, seems to have accepted them pretty well and doesn't mind any more when they are roaming around the garden.
My language skills in German are pretty poor, but I can just about manage the basics, so if you wish to communicate in German be patient with me.
My partner Stephen and I look forward to meeting you soon.

The Fumbally Cafe is one of the coolest cafes in Dublin, and you are just a short walk from the center of town - St Stephen's Green, Grafton Street and Temple Bar. The main tourist attractions are within an easy walking distance from here. The main train and bus stations are within easy walking distance as is the nearest Luas station (light rail system). I'm from here and know this city and the country very well so feel free to ask me about anywhere you'd like to go or about things you'd like to do.

neighborhood_overview: The neighbourhood is a very special place.  It is a small enclave with Victorian era cottages and redbrick houses that looks pretty much as it did when built in the 1890s.  It is a "cul de sac" (no through traffic) so it is very quiet and peaceful.  It is right across from the large and beautiful Phoneix Park that is home to Ireland's President and also the zoo.  The zoo is so close that you can here the lions and monkeys from the cottage!   There are great cafes and restaurants within a few minutes walk, including a traditional pub that won Ireland's "pub of the year" award. This location is amazing with lots of museums and attractions within a short walk, the fresh air and space of the Phoneix Park and only a 25 minute walk along the river to Temple Bar.
notes: Past guests love that the cottage is near to many cultural attractions and right on the edge of the beautiful Phoneix Park.  It is a perfect location for those who enjoy walking in the city and being close to nature by the Phoneix Park and the River Liffey.   The neighbourhood is quiet and friendly - guest get to experience a real Dublin community.  The area is a pleasant 20 minute walk along the river from the Temple Bar area.  It is very easy to explore the city from this location though I'd advise visitors who are interested in the "drinking culture" of the Temple Bar area, to book accommodation in that part of the city instead of our lovely, quiet neighbourhood!
transit: There are many attractions in the immediate neighbourhood and the "center" of the city is a pleasant 20 minute walk along the river.   There are great transport links.  We are a 5 minute walk from Heuston Station, one of the main train/bus/tram stations in Dublin. There is a direct airport bus to and from Heuston station and the Luas (tram) plus many buses run to the city centre, its just a 5 minute ride. There is a "Dublin Bikes" bike hire station  at Heuston station and the sight-seeing buses also pass and stop there. There is on-street parking available outside the house at no cost. If planning to use public transport, consider buying a "LEAP" card on arrival that includes bus/tram/DART/commuter trains and the Airlink airport bus.  Prices: 24 hours €10, 3 days (72 hours) €19.50, 7 days (168 hours) €40.  Available to buy at the Spar shop in Dublin airport.

interaction: Either myself or my partner Wellington will meet guests on arrival to welcome them and to provide a tour of the house and provide advice on the best things to do and visit in Dublin and Ireland.   The hosts will not be present in the house while guests are staying but will be available by phone/email if needed.
house_rules: This is an authentic and friendly Dublin community and neighbourhood and we ask guests to respect the house and our neighbours. Alcohol abuse, drug taking, loud music and parties strictly not permitted. The house is non-smoking and pets are not permitted. Smoking is possible in the backyard smoking area. Where a booking is made for a couple, the main downstairs bedroom is prepared and the second bedroom is not accessible.  Please specify if two rooms are required. Please take care with the toilet and do not flush anything other than toilet paper to avoid blocked pipes. Please treat and care for the house as your own.  Guests must leave the house tidy and to wash up their own dishes and to strip beds and leave bed linen and towels in the corner of the bedroom for laundering. If you notice any problems, please notify us straight away so we can rectify.
host_about:
I'm a Dubliner who grew up in south Dublin and I've been happily living in this great part of the north city center for the past 10 years.  I am well travelled and have visited many European countries, Asia, Australia and the USA.  I lived in France for a year and a half and lived in Australia for two years.

I really love Dublin as a city to live in and to explore and hang out.  There is a great mix of old and new, tradition and change in Dublin and a great atmosphere, nightlife and lots of events.  The city has beautiful parks, rivers and waterways and is nestled between the sea, mountains and lots of green countryside.

I enjoy the outdoors  hillwalking, surfing, camping and I have recently been spending more time in Wicklow (south of Dublin) improving my horse-riding.

Either myself of my partner Wellington will be available to welcome you.  We are delighted to give advice to guests and share our knowledge of Dublin and Ireland.

My personal motto: It is all about having good intentions and creating good experiences with people. Oh, and, follow your dreams because life is short.

There are excellent pubs and restaurants to suit all tastes. Parks, museums and galleries all within a short stroll. Herbert Park -  Next door Herbert Park is a green oasis spread over 32 acres of prime Ballsbridge land. It is named after Sidney Herbert, the father of the Earl of Pembroke who owned the land that Ballsbridge was built on. notes: Sláinte and welcome to Dublin! Let yourself be charmed by the city famous for its pub culture and literary tradition. Enjoy a pint of Guinness or a tumbler of Jameson at one of Dublin's more than 1,000 pubs. Experience the festive St Patrick's Day in March or the Writer's Festival in May celebrating contemporary writers as well as the literary heritage of world famous writers such as Samuel Beckett, WB Yeats and James Joyce. Revel in the vibrant live music scene, from arena to clubs to the streets of Dublin. Get a kick out of the charming cobblestoned Temple Bar neighborhood filled to the brim with cafés, art galleries and architectural grandeur.  Up for a game of Gaelic football or Hurling? Then Croke Park is the place for you, the fourth biggest sport's venue in Europe. Take a walk down to the bustling Moore Street market or relax in one of Dublin's many parks or take a ride with Dublin Bus Guided Sightseeing Tours. I love living in this city and I love living so close to the action.
It really is a 15 minute walk to the centre - I consider George's St the start of the action. (If your Guide book is saying the centre is O'Connell St, then maybe officially yeah, but you wouldn't want to hang out there. Trust me, it's George's Street) Food, music, shopping, coffee, people watching - all taken care of in that area
St. Patrick's Cathedral is nearby with the park adjoining it. And up the hill from that is Christchurch. 
I love food - eating it, cooking, buying it, having people over, so I adore that right by the house is a Lidl supermarket with great fresh produce - the fruit and veg are great and they usually have a selection of fresh fish too. 
Not to mention the bakery which bakes all day!
It's so easy to fall out of bed, round the corner and get whatever I need. Even after a big night out.
They have a good selection of beer and wine too.


This is a small city so I bike everywhere, the Dublin City bikes are great if you're a visitor. There are stations everywhere. But I think what visitors mostly say about this city is how accessible it is, you really can walk everywhere (well, to most of the worth seeing places)



Before considering booking please note:
I do actually live in this little house, most of the time so it's only available when I'm on holidays or at weekends (I'll go stay with friends or my parents)
I will try to consider any requests that I get. I know how tough it is to get a nice place in a capital city.
Please let me know when you'll be arriving so that I can do my best to be available or get a keyholder to be there. This isn't always possible as I work 9 to 5 Monday to Friday. 

I'm mentioning this because it's a question I got asked, but yes bed linen and towels are provided!
Please let me know how many are staying and I'll leave out plenty.

I provide shampoo, conditioner, showergel, toothpaste and face wipes also.

There are notes in the house for the heating, hot water and wifi password.

There's usually tea, coffee, condiments, oils, dressings, spices, herbs and basic food stuffs in the house (rice, pasta, noodles, cous cous, beans) - please feel free to use any of it .... if it's there!
And if there's anything in the fridge at all, and you like the look of it, help yourself.

host_about:
From Dublin, Ireland. Retired Civil Engineer, living with my wife Cathy and our three young adult children, when they are not living away from home. 
Our primary interests are; cycling, hiking, skiing, travel, cooking and gardening and of course our dog Barney.
We often host dinner parties  for family and/or friends, so we are well accustomed to catering for guests, often including overnight stays- we cook traditional Irish food as well as Indian, Italian, Spanish, Middle Eastern and Asian among others. We also like eating out at local or City restaurants of all cuisines.
We quite frequently travel abroad and in recent times have been to France (Skiing), Vietnam, Istanbul, Poland (Krakow & Zakopane), Slovakia, Hungary (Budapest) and Lanzarote ( Canary Islands), where we love meeting foreign people and enjoying their culture, architecture and cuisine. 
We love most  classical music( including modern minimalists) and jazz as well as modern popular music etc and have a vast collection of CD's and vinyl.
We like foreign cinema especially French and Nordic Noir and often visit the local specialist cinema in Dun Laoghaire (The Pavilion Theatre) where they have weekly showings. We also like BBC4 TV Foreign Series such as Borgen, The Killing, The Bridge and Spiral.
Our reading interests are varied and we have a vast array of books in our house from classics, travel, exploration to Nordic Noir such as Nesbo, Mankell and Larssen.
Our life mottos are; to live and enjoy life to the full and age is just a number

We are very close to lovely parks at Bushy Park and Marley Park and there is a lovely walk nearby which follows the River Dodder. host_about:
I would consider myself to be a citizen of the world and therefore feel that life for me is all about the experiences and memories that you treasure, those that you continually look back on and have pleasure in talking about.

To that end travelling has become a passion and fuels my desire to experience different cultures and societies, above all it allows me to meet different people and create those memories.

When visiting different Countries however comfort is everything to me so I love food (of course) but often get into trouble trying to experiment with unknown dishes but don't worry I always make up for that by enjoying local wines (funnily enough always white) and cocktails.

Where would the World be without cocktails or come to think about it "liquor of any type" if your willing to try anything just that once.

The endless amount of destinations to choose from and the history, architecture and culture open to us amazes me, I always find myself re-evaluating my lifestyle and personal choices once I've been away and continually feel grateful in terms of what I have and the possibilities available to any individual if she or he puts his / her mind to it. 

Love meeting new people especially if they have interesting life stories or are from different warps of life, they always appear to have a different or more open aspect on the world or it seems life in general.

Couldn't live without an iron, a smart phone, a credit card, a comfortable pair of shoes or more importantly my partner who will always be the love of my life and hopefully soon to be wife. 

Favorite destination impossible to choose from, to many I've seen and want to go back to and to many still left to see and already on my listof must dos.

Books give me, action, espionage or mob related, probably the same with movies, although, every now and again something that will bring a tear to my eye most recently being The Help or The Bucket List or a classic The Shawshank Redemption etc. 

In terms of being a host I try to provide guests with any and everything they might possibly need to make their stay more enjoyable and comfortable, the more information I can provide the better, always good to no what is available locally and where to go if you need something, from the closest and best restaurant to renting a vehicle at a competitive rate, the nearest Church or good watering hole. 

Dublin is one of the most amazing cities in the world as everything is so accessible, the mountains or a beach all a 20 minute drive away or easily available to you via public transport.

As a major European city you will find a constant and endless abundance of culture and entertainment available to you. I just hope you have enough time to experience it all and if not it will just give you an excuse to return.

Clontarf is close to Dublin city centre and it's a 10 minute walk to the coast (Clontarf Promenade) from our house. The city centre is a 15 minute walk away, along one of the most elegant Georgian streetscapes in the world and through the beautiful St. Stephen's Green park. neighborhood_overview: Our neighbourhood is super central but has still a lot of old-world charm - walking 10 minutes in any direction can take you to totally different worlds - on one side there's the river and the city Docklands and Finance district. If you keep walking up the river you soon reach the heart of the city and it is a lovely walk especially at night. 10 minutes in the other direction and you are in a lovely park with swings and a good sized playground 10 mins in another direction and you are on the seafront promenade in the nice neighbourhood of Clontarf with the Yacht Bar. The bird sanctuary and beach at Bull Island are just a short drive away, as is St. Anne's Park with its riverside walks and famous rose gardens and Sunday market. There is a large supermarket around the corner as well as a smaller supermarket, post office and pharmacy within 5 mins of our front door. Our neighbourhood is a really good mix of old and new, extremely convenient and central. We love it here and we hope you will
notes: This is a very old house (built 1892) and it's been fully remodelled (new wiring, insulation, heating and plumbing) but we have deliberately retained some of its original features and fittings including the original flooring. This space is our home a lot of the time so it is not a 'beige' corporate let . For that reason we leave our books, music etc for you to enjoy and the furniture and fixtures especially beds, bed linens and towels are of a very high standard.
transit: Max 30 mins to Trinity College gates from our house and a really nice walk by the river passing through Docklands area with cafes and restaurants. DART (Suburban train) 10 mins walk from our house can take you to Dublin's coastal villages of Howth (with its famous hill to climb giving you an excellent view of the city, and many lovely fresh fish restaurants) or take the train to the south coast villages of Dun Laoighire and Dalkey (home of many Irish celebrities). interaction: If you take the whole house one or both of us will meet you on arrival and hopefully also on departure.  Otherwise we stay in Dublin sometimes but we also like to travel too. We have a country house we go to when you are in our house or else we go away for the weekend - basically we use Air BnB a lot too so we hope that we are as good hosts as we would like to meet :) We will respect your privacy and will be happy to answer any questions you might have. If we are not there then we will always  be just a phone call away for whatever you need. For many years we have exchanged our home with people from all over the world so we are well aware of what people need in a place to stay and do our best to provide a 'home away from home'.
house_rules: No heeled shoes indoors as we have solid wood floors Do not adjust heating settings - we will pre-set them to meet your requests and we will also show you how to 'boost' for an additional hour at a time but if you amend the timing or programmes on our heating system we will deduct costs of all the extra heating - (this is because we have had one or two very negative experiences where people left heating 24/7 and our bill exceeded the cost of the stay) If more than normal cleaning required  50 euros will be deducted from deposit - for example in over 100 lets it has happened once that guests damaged towels badly they had to be replaced and a set of guests did not clean any dishes or pots or pans in the kitchen having stayed for a week - but that is 2 out of 100 so 98% have no problems. It's the archetypal Dublin red brick terrace that is very central and alive with city living.  Phoenix Park – the largest in-city park in the world – is literally on your doorstep, and is also home to Dublin Zoo. Dublin’s biggest tourist attraction – the Guinness Storehouse – is a few  minutes walk, as well as other big names such as the Jameson  Distillery, the Irish Museum of Modern Art and the Four Courts.

The buses and the LUAS city tram can bring you directly to the city centre in approximately 20 mins. There is a very close bus stop right across from the house on Infirmary Road for the 46A bus route.  Walking to the city centre (O’Connell Bridge) takes 30 minutes, where you’ll pass several landmarks you won’t want to miss during your stay. Collins Barracks, Jameson Distillery, James Joyce Museum and the Spire. Temple Bar, famous for it’s nightlife, is again about 30 minutes walk, along the Liffey and crossing the famous Ha'penny Bridge.

neighborhood_overview: I live in a great part of town - really old neighbourhood. My house dates from 1892 :-) But we are right next to one of the city's newest neighbourhoods in Docklands. We are super accessible to everywhere - especially the concert halls and conference centre and we also have a decent selection of restaurants and two large supermarkets nearby for when you want to eat in.  Easy to get to and from with walking or public transport and taxis home are super cheap if you have a late night and want to be dropped at the door. We're very close to the airport as well just 20 mins in a cab.
notes: It is an old house - we've fully refurbished it but there are old parts - like stripped pine floorboards - to us this is part of the charm - we would ask you to treat these unique aspects with care. The heating has automatic pre-sets but anytime you need it you can add another hour's heating by pressing a boost button and turning on the heat at source in your bedroom. On the other hand if you are too warm you can turn off the heater at source in your bedroom.
transit: 151 bus stops at the end of my street, a LUAS tram is a little further on, and the airport bus stops at the convention centre (about 10 mins walk away). Taxis to the centre are cheap but it is equally easy to walk up the river - you can be in front of Trinity College in about 20-25 mins from my front door. It's not too far to the beach from my house if you're interested and there's a park nearby with swings and a playground for children.
access: King-sized bedroom with wifi, bathroom with power shower- we always offer the kitchen for breakfast but it is NOT available for other meals unless in the case of a long stay (6 days or more) and only by mutual arrangement. interaction: As much or as little interaction as you want really.  We are both friendly and open people who are working professionals. neighborhood_overview: Chapelizod is a medieval village preserved within the city of Dublin, Ireland. It lies within the wooded valley of the River Liffey, near the Strawberry Beds and the Phoenix Park. Interesting buildings in the village include the church of St Laurence (Church of Ireland) with its medieval bell tower (12 century). A fine Georgian house where Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu wrote, stands at the corner of Church Lane facing Main Street in front of this church. The renovated old RIC barracks on Main Street predates the old Constabulary, serving as an army barracks from the reign of William and Mary.  The nearby Phoenix Park was laid out by the Dukes of Ormond as a deer park and a large heard still occupy the park. It is delightful location for walks and picnics. neighborhood_overview: Dublin north side of the Liffey is a vibrant multicultural place where the old city and the new one collide. From Asian and African markets and shops to the old pubs and streets of the city, the apartment is right in the middle of it. It's actually built over a large mall and 4 major supermarket chains are less than a minute's walk from the door. It sits across the road from a Dublin Bike stand and all public transport options are no more than a few minutes away. Otherwise the entire city takes 25 minutes to walk across. One of Ireland's major shopping streets Henry Street is 3 minutes walk away and contains malls, department stores and specialist shops. I love this city. It's very small, very friendly and there are a ton of things to do outside the door. So go and explore.
notes: Very fast internet but no TV. Otherwise the flat has every amenity you'll need. I have left all of the basics in the kitchen. Teas [normal and herbal], Coffee [Nespresso with plenty of complimentary capsules and instant], Milk, Olive Oil, Salt, Pepper and other condiments. Actually pretty much all you'll need for your stay. Because of the age and height [5th floor] of the building you can shower [It's not a power shower just a regular one] perfectly well but the bath doesn't fill and has never been used. On the plus side I'm providing soaps, towels, shampoo, conditioner and various other useful things like toilet paper. The bed is soft. I mean very soft. I would suggest you consider that in advance before booking. There is an excellent exercise bike in the living room if you wish to work up a bit of a sweat. It is at your disposal if you would like to use it. Any other questions please don't hesitate to contact me. By the way there is a Didgeridoo and an instruction book on how to use

Please note that Parnell Street is pretty chaotic at the moment due to the building of the light railway track (LUAS). This is due to be finished by the end of the year.

neighborhood_overview: Sandymount is one of the most beautiful urban villages in Dublin with the city centre just being a stone's throw away, while still boasting a beautiful coastal promenade. It has the beautiful combination of being peaceful yet central. Sandymount village has upmarket restaurants, famous coffee shops, boutiques, supermarkets, organic food stores, butchers, pubs, cricket grounds, bike shops & rental, a bookie shop, hairdressers and two pharmacies. The Aviva stadium and RDS are both within 5 minute walks along with Bath Avenue where you will find many popular Irish pubs for young and old. The Bord Gais theatre and Grand Canal are both within 10 minute walks or 3 minutes in a taxi. The 3Arena (formerly 02 / Point Depot) is a 20 minute walk or 5 minutes in a taxi. The Ballsbridge business / embassy district including the US embassy is within 2.4km of my house. Merrion Square and the National Gallery are 20 minute walks away whilst Stephen's Green and Grafton Street are 30 minute walks away.
notes: Hi, I'm Mark. I bought this beautiful house in August 2012 and have spent a good deal of time having it restored and modernised but also keeping some of its origins (window shutters, fireplaces, cute staircases and doors to bedrooms along with the front door). I work as an Investment Manager in my family's business. I like to travel a lot and spend a good few weekends of the year travelling Ireland.  I am a keen sportsman and I love golf! I use sport to relax. I grew up in Killiney which is south Dublin and again, very close to the sea. I enjoy spending time back home with my parents and siblings. I have been told many times how beautiful and warm my house is and I am very proud of it.
transit: Public transport is on your doorstop. The DART (Dublin train service) is within 700 meters of my house. With this, you can travel out as far south as Bray & Greystones (passing by beautiful scenic and historical areas such as Dalkey & Killiney) and you can travel as far north as Howth (passing through central town on your way). The Bus stop is a 30 second walk away and beside the Bus stop is a taxi rank.    The Aircoach service from Dublin airport to Greystones (route 702) passes right by Sandymount. This runs on an hourly basis and costs €13 for a return trip. A taxi from the airport will cost you roughly €30 and if you catch me on a lucky day you might receive a lift from myself! I'm happy to offer you help on booking transport though so please just ask.

neighborhood_overview: The warren of streets around the apartment is home to Irish design stores, independent cafés, vintage shops, a slew of new restaurants and some of the city's best pubs. It's got a real neighbourhood feel even though you are right in the middle of the city centre.  Stephen's Green, Trinity College and Merrion Sq are all close by if you need some green space. Fallon & Byrne, Dublin's equivalent of Dean & Deluca is right across the road for when you need to stock up on artisinal Irish produce. Dunnes Supermarket is directly beside more front door for any other groceries you might need.
notes: The apartment is on the second floor of a beautiful old building in Dublin. Unfortunately it doesn't have a lift so it is not suitable for wheelchair users. If you have lots of cases it will be a bit of a chore lugging them up the second floor, sorry about that! The apartment is right in the middle of the city-centre, you will never need a taxi and you can walk everywhere. There are lots of great bars and restaurants on our doorstep which is very handy. But the central location means that you will hear some street noise in the living areas of the apartment at night time (the bedroom is at the back of the building which is quieter and many of our guests are amazed by how peaceful it is).
transit: The apartment is a 3 minute walk from the Aircoach and Airlink 747 bus stops (Trinity/College Green) which service the airport. A taxi from the airport takes about 25 minutes depending on traffic and costs about €20+. Dublin's tram is called The Luas and it's a 5 minute walk to both lines (Jervis and Stephen's Green). There's a multi storey car park around the corner on Drury St. Book online in advance and this costs €14 a day. We are lucky to have a Dublin Bikes station right across the road. The light rail system that runs along Dublin Bay is called The Dart and Tara St, the closest station is a ten minute walk. Dublin is full of taxis and there's a rank around the corner on George's St in front of Dunnes Stores. Connolly Train Station is about a 15 minute walk away on the north side of the river. Heuston Rail Station is accessed via buses on Aston Quay or by taking the Luas (Jervis stop).

neighborhood_overview: This is a small tree-lined street along the Royal Canal in the north inner city, just off one of the main arteries into Dublin. It's on the edge of the inner city so while it's a quiet location, it's still only 20 minutes walk to the Spire, which marks the city centre. The apartment is facing the canal on a slight rise, it has a light airy aspect with a great view over the rooftops of the north city. The area is an old Dublin inner city neighbourhood with a mix of newcomers and Dubliners who have lived here for generations. As one of the older residential streets in the city centre, this is the real inner city, working class Dublin that tourists rarely see. As one guest said in a review 'the location is safe, but it doesn't look very appealing'! There's a small grocery shop about a hundred yards away and a lovely little Italian restaurant that also does excellent take-away pizza.
notes: We have a dog, a very friendly little spaniel called Flurry, but he is not in the apartment — he lives downstairs with us.
transit: The location is perfect for exploring the city. A 20 minute walk will take you into the city centre and 10/15 minutes walking brings you to the main transport hub — Connolly train station for mainline, commuter and light rail and Busarus (the main bus station). A short bus or train ride from here will get you to the RDS exhibition/showgrounds and the Aviva stadium. Croke Park stadium is 5 minutes walk and the Dublin Convention centre about 20 minutes walk away. There are also many buses in and out of the city, the bus stop is about 100 yards from the front door. There is free on-street parking outside the house. If you want to explore Dublin city it really is not necessary to have a car for your stay here. host_about:
From Dublin, Ireland. Retired Civil Engineer, living with my wife Cathy and our three young adult children, when they are not living away from home. 
Our primary interests are; cycling, hiking, skiing, travel, cooking and gardening and of course our dog Barney.
We often host dinner parties  for family and/or friends, so we are well accustomed to catering for guests, often including overnight stays- we cook traditional Irish food as well as Indian, Italian, Spanish, Middle Eastern and Asian among others. We also like eating out at local or City restaurants of all cuisines.
We quite frequently travel abroad and in recent times have been to France (Skiing), Vietnam, Istanbul, Poland (Krakow & Zakopane), Slovakia, Hungary (Budapest) and Lanzarote ( Canary Islands), where we love meeting foreign people and enjoying their culture, architecture and cuisine. 
We love most  classical music( including modern minimalists) and jazz as well as modern popular music etc and have a vast collection of CD's and vinyl.
We like foreign cinema especially French and Nordic Noir and often visit the local specialist cinema in Dun Laoghaire (The Pavilion Theatre) where they have weekly showings. We also like BBC4 TV Foreign Series such as Borgen, The Killing, The Bridge and Spiral.
Our reading interests are varied and we have a vast array of books in our house from classics, travel, exploration to Nordic Noir such as Nesbo, Mankell and Larssen.
Our life mottos are; to live and enjoy life to the full and age is just a number

Hi we're Paul and Mary. 
This is our spacious modernised redbrick home in the quiet but very centrally located Sandymount area. It's Dublin's best neighbourhood with the sea on your doorstep and the city just 15 minutes walk away. 
Sandymount Strand is the most famous beach in Irish fiction, James Joyce based two episodes of his epic novel Ulysses here, writing: "Am I walking into eternity along Sandymount strand?"
If you don't feel like walking, the number 1 bus passes the top of the road to bring you straight to the heart of the city in minutes.  The Dart (light rail) is a six minute walk from the house. It brings you out to the pretty seaside towns and villages of Howth, Dalkey and Killiney where you can stroll around the shops and sample the local seafood. 
The house is more than 100 years old, a charming redbrick terrace in a family neighbourhood- overlooking the Dodder river. 
The home of Irish rugby, and the oldest international ground in world rugby, Lansdowne Road (The Aviva Stadium) is on our doorstep.  Dublin's silicon docks, home to (Hidden by Airbnb) , (Hidden by Airbnb) , (Hidden by Airbnb) , Airbnb and Dublin's convention centre is a ten minute stroll.  The RDS - home to the legendary Dublin Horse Show is also nearby.  At either end of our street are some of the best bars and restaurants in Dublin, including Slattery's, The Vintage Inn, Juniors, The Old Spot and Farmer Browns.  The picturesque village of Sandymount has nice little shops, cafes and lovely restaurants for a very easy and relaxed night out. 
We have lovingly restored the house ourselves- keeping as much of its old charm as possible. 
We love our home and hope you will too.  It's bright and spacious (130 sq metres) but still warm and cosy.  We have a country style kitchen, solid oak floors and a stove for burning wood and traditional Irish turf. Perfect for a winter's night! It's a great house for reading, relaxing and having a glass of wine after a day out seeing the sights of Dublin.

A little bit about us: We are college friends who first met while studying in Dublin City University, now we're married!
Travelling is our passion.  We've been all over Europe, the US & Canada, South America, Africa, Australia and Asia.  Antarctica is the only continent we haven't made it to yet.  But there's still time! Italy is our favourite place to visit, but we also love New York, Buenos Aires, Madrid and Sydney.  We spent our wonderful honeymoon on safari in Kenya.
We are easy going and fun and like meeting new people and would also love people to enjoy our home in our absence!

host_about:
Hello!
I'm Jen. I'm from Dublin born and bred. I'm a proud Dub. I LOVE my city. I hope you will too. 

My day job is in Television Production. I love music - I go to gigs all the time. I also love the cinema, dining out, spending time with my family and going to Dublin's many, many brilliant pubs.  

I've travelled quite a bit. I've been to quite a few American cities including New York (my favourite city to visit), Boston, Memphis, Austin, L.A., San Antonio, New Orleans, Houston, San Diego, Honolulu, San Francisco, Vegas and Portland. I love what I've seen of Canada too. I've travelled a little bit in Australia and New Zealand (my favourite country to visit). And of course I've seen lots of Europe too.  

As much as i love travelling there's no where I'd rather be than Ireland, and in particular Dublin. We're a small, walkable city that's bursting at the seams with culture and history. We have beautiful beaches, forests and mountains. And some of the best pubs in the world! Did i mention the pubs?? :) Whenever i have friends coming to visit from abroad i always tell them to avoid the tourist traps like Temple Bar. There are plenty of other places to spend your time and hard earned money, places where you're more likely to experience the real Dublin.   I have lots of suggestions to share! 

I'm an easy going person. I would like any guests staying in my home to treat it with respect as they would their own.

The Vikings founded the city just behind the building in the site now known as Dubh Linn Gardens at Dublin Castle which is a pretty spot in which to get some respite and sunshine if there's any going, amidst the lovely shrubs to the sound of cascading water. Temple Bar district is just across the street with its lively pubs and street performers but best of all is the Saturday morning farmers' market on Meeting House Square. My favourite for coffee is either Kaph on Drury Street or Fallon & Byrne Food Emporium on Exchequer Street. My current favourite restaurant is L'Gueleton on Fade Street as well as the more mediatised and hyped Fade Street Social. neighborhood_overview: When I was growing up this stretch of the quays was full of book and antique shops, interspaced with solicitors offices (the Four Courts are just upstream). In the second half of the 20th. C, there were plans to demolish the historic buildings and widen the roads. It was left to decay, much as the opposite side of the river - Temple Bar, had done. Capel Street, around the corner is one of my favorite places in the city- still a mixture of tool shops, great value food and a bit of everything else thrown in. The fruit and veg. market is around the corner too- well worth a visit if you're interested in a bit of old Dublin.
notes: The bedrooms are generally very quiet -no traffic noise or street shenanigans. Much of the structure is up to 300 years old, so you can expect to hear the neighbours downstairs. The water pressure is low - don't expect a vigorous shower, (I will try to upgrade in the very near future).  The place is located beside the "Tea Garden", which is a cool place to hang out if you want to drink unusual teas and smoke shisha- this accounts for the ambient music and smell of incense at the street!

Most of the best Tourist attractions are within walking distance, others may be accessed easily by public transport. notes: No smoking, and no pets permitted in the building. CAR PARKING:  unless you plan to leave Dublin a car is unnecessary and we strongly suggest alternative methods of transport (your legs will suffice in 90% of cases)

My daughter Martha attends college in Dublin during the week and stays in the house during the weekdays so she is also around to help with anything guests might need if I am not available myself.
house_rules: We would expect guests to respect our property and belongings and leave it as found. Smoking is not allowed on the premises.
host_about: I moved here to Sligo with my family over 6 years ago for a better quality of life and we really love where we live. Would describe myself as sociable and really interested in people. My husband and I have always been very involved with the arts so we enjoy good conversations about art, literature film and politics. The Saturday Guardian is one of the highlights  of my week but regrettably, I don't always have the time or the patience to cook all those recipes that I keep cutting out. I cook great soup, French Onion, Roasted Red Pepper  and Cassoulet are amongst my specialities! I have lived in Belgium and Holland so can still converse in French though my Dutch needs a little brushing up. Can't live without literature and music but have put off 'War and Peace' for the last ten years. Now ready to embark on this great literary adventure. Would welcome conversations on same with any airbnb guest with an interest in Tolstoy. Despite some 'highbrow' tastes I also have a passion for popular fiction; I just finished Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's 'Americanah',  riveting.

host_about: I love where I live in Dublin. By the Phoenix Park, and right in to the city with a quick bus ride. I love an unshowy town in the Costa Brava called L'estartit. I love Joan's ( he's a Catalan!) restaurant in   tiny medieval St. Marti d'Empuries nearby. I love A Suitable Boy by Vikram Seth, and read it all over again every 2 or 3 years. I love water in all forms, and especially swimming. I'm part of a triathlon club, and love the group sessions. I love Out of Africa, The English Patient, The Proposition, Apocalypto, Charlie & The Chocolate Factory ( with Gene Wilder ). I love contemporary dance, and theatre that is really inventive/engaging/experiential. Travelling, I like to connect with my host, and to compliment them on their hospitality. I like to sit back and enjoy what they have laid on. If anything minor could be better, I prefer to let them know discreetly, rather than posting in a review. Hosting-wise, I want my guests to have a sense that they can really make themselves at home, that the personality and warmth of our house comes through. And that I have given them a good intro to everything when I meet them. And will be available or have help available if anything crops up. Life motto...Hmm...that's a funny one! As a recovering perfectionist...I like Sheryl Sandberg's : Done is better than perfect ;0)

space: Captain's Quarters is a modern 2 bed apartment in an 18th century Historic Barracks right beside the National Print Museum. neighborhood_overview: The house is located in the small village of Donabate in North County Dublin over looking the village green. Although it's just around the corner from the centre of the village, it is set back from the road on a quiet street. When you step out the front door you can walk to the supermarket in 3 minutes. The train station is also just 3 minutes walk away and a train takes 25 minutes to bring you to the centre of Dublin City. The long sandy beach of Donabate is 20 minutes walk away or instead of turning right onto the beach you could turn left and walk along the cliffs to another small secluded beach or another long sandy beach in Portrane.  Another favourite walk of ours is to and around Newbridge House and Park which has a super playground for kids as well as a visitors farm.  Dublin Airport is 12 minutes drive southbound on the M1 motorway. Head north on the M1 and Belfast is 2 hours drive away with lots of interesting, historical and picturesque places along the way.

Travel 4 minutes by train to get to the seaside village of Malahide which is an especially nice place to go for something to eat or drink. If you've hired a car, the M1 motorway is 4 minutes drive away and the M50 is 10 minutes drive.

When this route was crossed by the then new circular road the village expanded rapidly into a city quarter but retained its village feel especially in its side streets and lanes. Local shopping includes supermarkets, convenience (one with 24hr opening) and speciality shops all within 5 mins walk. name: Bayview  - a Georgian Cottage
summary: Built in 1832, Bayview is a fusion of modern and historical in a cosy protected cottage. Bayview Ave is a cultural oasis, with eclectic neighbours. The airport, city centre, coast, train and bus stations, are all only 20 mins away. Family friendly.
space: 50 Bayview Ave was built in 1832 to house a naval officer working in the customs house on the River Liffey. A servant lived in the basement and catered to the needs of the officer using a bell system. The house is a protected structure because of it's architectural significance. It is one of only 8,600 protected structures in Dublin city. Bayview has unique period features: a marble fireplace, window shutters, high ceilings, railed gardens and many more. There is 240Mb/s internet. Bayview has a cot, a stroller, a high chair and a play desk for children to use.

interaction: Whilst we both work, often one of us is working from home and would be around to answer any questions about the lodge or the surrounding area.  If we aren't then it's just a phone call to get an answer.

This house dates from 1864 'The Victorian Period'.   As one would expect in a neighborhood of this vintage, the resident profile is a mixed one and is ever changing. Many local families have lived in the area for generations. In more recent times the area has become popular with younger professionals and students from the nearby colleges of technology, law, and English language. There is a sizable immigrant population - particularly eastern Europeans. The city center boundary is just around the corner and the city's main street with all the top stores, bars, cafes, and restaurants is just a ten-minute walk away.   The area is generally safe and quiet. Weekends can be a little busier with more car and foot traffic than during the week but this is to be expected as people make their way home after socializing in the city center.

We have the Guinness Storehouse less than a minute walk way and the historic Christchurch Cathedral a 5 minute walk away. One of Ireland's most famous revolutionary heros (Robert Emmet), met his end outside St Catherine's church at the end of our street. There are many cafes, shops and pubs within a couple of minutes walk. Many public transport routes pass very closely. Our back garden overlooks a heritage park and all the sights in Dublin are within walking distance.
notes: Our house is within really easy walking distance of all the sights in Dublin - both in the direction of the city (10 minutes walk) as well as towards Europe's largest city Park, the Phoenix Park, which is only a 15 minute walk away. A free 'Dublin bikes' stand is at the corner. But there is no need for public transport really as all the sights are within easy walking distance. Ireland's gateway railway station to the west and south ( Heuston Station) is a 12 minute walk for when you want to get away on an overnight-trip or tour.
