Trinity College, one of the seven ancient universities of Britain and Ireland’s oldest university, is only a 5-minute walk away. After the fashion of the Dublin Georgian squares, featuring a park in the centre: Crosthwaite Park was completed between 1860 and 1875. The unique quality of 19th century Dun Laoghaire is the result of two products of the Steam Age  , the steam ship and the railway ( Now the DART Trainline). Dun Laoghaire’s 19th century past paints a good picture of the Victorian way of life, and much of this is well reflected in the buildings of the town.

neighborhood_overview: Donnycarney (Irish: Domhnach Cearnach, meaning Carney's Church) is a Northside suburb in the city of Dublin, Ireland. It is bordered by Beaumont, Artane, Killester and Marino, and lies in the postal districts of Dublin 3, 9 and 5. Donnycarney is a mostly residential area, located 5km from the centre of Dublin. It has a good range of amenities including restaurants, a credit union, a community youth project in the newly built community centre, and a 3.25ha park, May Park (Donnycarney Park). The area is crossed by one of Dublin's "small rivers". Donnycarney is most notable as the home of Parnell Park, a Gaelic Athletic Association stadium where the Dublin inter-county teams play many of their matches, including lower-profile matches which do not warrant the use of Croke Park, the national stadium. neighborhood_overview: St Anne's is a quite and mature estate. North Bull Island National Nature Reserve is on the other side of St Anne's park, idea for wild life, bird watching or a long walk. Raheny junction is 700m away on Howth Road,  with a local super market(Super Value),  pharmacies, butcher, flower shop, dry cleaner, banks, gym and number of restaurants. Life motto?  So many.... 

Live for the day
Seize the moment
One mans rubbish is another mans treasure  (I like to recycle!)

Why lie awake thinking about it; just get up and do it!

neighborhood_overview: The beauty of Chapelizod is its rural village setting,only 3+ miles from the heart of Dublin City. And with six bus routes at a three-minute walk, you're well positioned to enjoy all the benefits of the city, without the hassle and expense of city centre accommodation.  My house overlooks the busy Main Street at the front, and a beautiful 18th century church at the back. In fact, the church and its quaint little churchyard is the setting of Sheridan LeFanu's famous Victorian crime/mystery novel 'The House by the Churchyard.'  At the end of the road is The Mullingar House pub, setting of James Joyce's masterpiece novel 'Finnegan's Wake.' Joyce lived across the road from my house with his father (who also worked in the village) at the turn of the century, and his 'A Painful Case' short story from 'Dubliners' is set in Chapelizod Village.
notes: The Villager Pub is a hotspot for literary enthusiasts. Its decor, relatively unchanged since the 1930s/40s, appears frozen in time. Live traditional music takes place at the weekend, and a very good pint of Guinness is always on tap - also their toasted sandwiches are very popular too!  The Phoenix Park is Europe's largest walled park, and is an incredible recreational facility, housing Dublin Zoo, the home of the Irish President, and literally thousands and thousands of acres of woodland for walking, running, cycling and general leisure. A private pedestrian entrance, for village residents, is located a three-minute walk from my front door.
transit: The village is serviced by six different buses (at one bus stop) on the bridge, four minutes' walk from my front door. All six busses go to the city Centre (appr. 15 minutes away), and come at a frequency of between 5 and 15 minutes, depending on the day/time.  Taxis can be phoned for, and are reasonably priced. Taxis to city centre are appr €12-15 depending on day/time, and a taxi to/from Dublin airport will typically cost between €25-35.
access: The Phoenix Park has a pedestrian entrance for the village's residents, less than three minutes' walk from my front door.  There are two convenience stores, a pharmacy, and the quaint and very popular Villager Pub, which has been operating for over 200 years, only a few doors away.  At the top of Knockmaroon Hill (15 minutes walk, or 3/4 minute drive) is the very popular Angler's Rest seafood restaurant, which serves excellent food (and traditional music) in a picturesque countryside setting.
house_rules: I would ask that guests don't wear shoes in the house, as the carpet upstairs is very good wool (royal blue) and marks easily.  Quiet, respectful guests are sought, who won't disrespect my neighbors. That said, the walls of this house are very solid, and there's certainly no need for whispering. I regularly play my piano in the evenings, without issue.  All of the furniture in this house is either new or antique, so I expect guests to treat the house and its belongings with respect.  Absolutely NO SMOKING in the house. No parties, no events.  No additional guests are permitted to be invited to/stay at the property without express permission from the house.
host_about:
Friendly Irish fellah here. I love literature, mainly Irish literature, which I studied, hence the reason for buying my house in Chapelizod, a village with a rich literary heritage, with links to James Joyce, Sheridan LeFanu, Bram Stoker, and the legend of Tristan and Iseult. 
I can also be found playing piano, singing in the shower, teaching college students, cooking and baking, and lots more besides.

With its own high street and a wealth of cool bars and restaurants as well as brilliant vintage shops.  BARS I think there are over 10 bars in Rathmines alone and then within minutes walk they're everywhere! The gorgeous Phoenix Park, one of the largest enclosed urban parks in Europe, is our favorite oasis as you can walk or ride a bicycle for miles and it's just a few minutes walk away. The Irish National War Memorial Gardens is also right next to our apartment. You can go for a stroll down by the bank of the Liffey and watch the local rowing teams practice throughout the spring and summer. Up the road lies Kilmainham, home to the Kilmainham Gaol and the Royal Hospital.  The former is now a museum and the later houses the Irish Museum of Modern Art. Both are well worth visiting. The people in our building and neighborhood are quiet and friendly. The area is safe and clean.

City Sightseeing buses stop nearby and will take you everywhere around the city. From Heuston you can even take a bus straight to and from the airport (Airlink 747 bus). Dublin is a young and vibrant capital so don't miss its nightlife and pub culture. And it's all happening just a couple of kilometres away. On Friday and Saturday the city is buzzing. neighborhood_overview: Like many cities Dublin is split in two with the River Liffey providing a clear division between the north and south sides of the city. We are located on a quiet street in the north, inner city Dublin. It was from this area that Georgian Dublin gained its roots and then spread throughout Dublin, something you'll easily spot in the local architecture. It may not have been as grand as the oppulent townhouses of the Southside but nearby you'll find there is a wealth of Georgian and Victorian architecture to see including Henrietta street, which is the earliest Georgian Street in Dublin and home to the Tenement Museum and Kings Inn. Other nearby attractions include Dublin's original reservoir - the basin, is just around the corner and its a lovely place to have a picnic and feed the ducks. There is a lovely playground located nearby. The Hugh Lane Gallery is located close by on Parnell Square.  Like most museums and galleries in Dublin admission is free. Dublin city centre is an easy walk

neighborhood_overview: Dublin 7 is a great part of Dublin and I really enjoy living here.  I regularly go running and walking in the Phoenix Park which is within a stones throw from my front door.  Stoneybatter, the lovely neighbourhood behind my housing estate has a number of new cafés with excellent barista coffee, for those who enjoy it! Some of my favourites are Slice, Love Supreme or Proper Order Coffee in Smithfield.  Likewise there are numerous modern eateries in the area, all the way in towards O' Connell street.  Tourist attractions abound: The Phoenix Park, The Guinness Storehouse, IMMA, The Royal Hospital and Kilmainham Gaol are all nearby within walking distance.  Otherwise the RHA, The National Gallery of Ireland, Hugh Lane Gallery are other excellent galleries for art lovers.  Shopping is endless, as are options for music, theatre and restaurants!

host_about:
Hello. I am an early thirties professional living in Dublin city centre. I have lived abroad in France for two years. I love France, its culture and language but I also love to visit other places too. Of the places I've visited so far Colombia, Bali, Vietnam and New York stand out for me. Countries I would still love to see are Japan and Iceland (among many others!) 
My other loves and interests include photography, flowers, art, cinema, great coffee, reading and music. I enjoy having people over for dinner, good food and good chats.

I practise yoga in a studio near my home in Dublin 7 and I love running and walking in the park by my house. It's free and the views are great!

I really enjoy meeting people when I travel and getting local recommendations too which is why I have enjoyed using airbnb myself. 

But while I enjoy travel, I am pretty passionate about Dublin and Ireland.
Ireland has great places to see and is rich in beautiful traditional music and culture and I would be delighted to share all the things that I think are special with my visitors.

neighborhood_overview: With its vibrant pub and restaurant scene and intimate village atmosphere, Ranelagh is one of Dublin's most fashionable addresses. The location can't be beaten, with Dublin City Centre on your doorstep and Dublin's Business District nearby. If you plan to experience one of Dublin's legendary Rugby weekends Aviva Stadium and the RDS are a 5-10 minute taxi drive away, or if your trip is for work, the Dublin 2 Business District is a short stroll away, with Barrow Street, Silicone Dock, the IFSC, the National Convention Centre and the RDS all easily accessible.
notes: Each of our six stylishly decorated Double Rooms is uniquely decorated, and named after a famous local legend to reflect the house's fascinating history. You can read more about the house and the people our Rooms are named after on the Ranelagh Rooms website, so whichever Room you book, you can soak up some local history during your visit. If you need more than one Room, just let us know and we will do our best to accommodate you.
transit: Ranelagh Rooms is the perfect place from which to explore the City, either on foot or by public transport. The City Centre is just a short stroll away, and Charlemont Luas (Tram) Stop and the No 44 and 61 buses are on your doorstep. GoCar Members can pick up their Rental Car just across the road from the house at the Northbrook Road GoCar Pick Up Station, and the nearest Dublin Bike Station is one block away at the Charlemont Luas Stop. Dublin Airport is a 14km drive, and easily accessible by Taxi, Bus, Aircoach and the Airlink Express. There is FREE on-street parking at weekends and evenings (Pay & Display during the day Monday - Friday). Guests can find extensive detailed information on How to Find Us, Getting To and From the Airport, Parking, and Dublin Public Transport on the Ranelagh Rooms website.
access: After booking Guests will receive a personal Keycode that will give them access to the property for the duration of their stay. The same code allows access to the Front Door, the Luggage Store and the Min Ryan Room.  Guests can enter the Front Door and Luggage Store from 7am on Day Of Arrival until 10pm on Day of Departure, and the Min Ryan Room from Check-in time of 3pm on Day of Arrival until Check-out time of 12pm on Day of Departure.
interaction: We use Smartlocks so that Guests can Check-in and Check-out at a time that suits them. We are always happy to provide a recommendation for where to eat, the best way to get around, etc; and you can find our extensive City Guide, as well as lots of useful Travel Information on the Ranelagh Rooms website. If you need anything we are always nearby, or at the end of the phone.

neighborhood_overview: The leafy residential suburb of Glasnevin is home to many famous Irish landmarks. The National Botanical Gardens, historic Glasnevin Cemetery, Dublin City University and even one of Dublin city's most famous pubs – The Gravediggers (est., 1833). John Kavanagh's (known to locals as the Gravediggers), beside the old Glasnevin Cemetery entrance on Prospect Square, is a mere 5 minute walk from your rental and has been run by eight generations of the Kavanagh family. The 19th-century charm of this pub has been maintained by the banning of televisions, radio and piped music. The pub's nickname is derived from the Gravediggers in the cemetery next door tapping on the side wall of the bar for a pint of plain on a break from their labours.

neighborhood_overview: Glenasmole valley is a haven for naturalists, hikers, hill-walkers, cyclists, artists and those seeking a healthy dose of nature and fresh air.  The valley is a special area of conservation and abounds with wildlife and wildflowers. We are situated on the Dublin Mountain Way (featured in the book: Top 1001 Walks You Must Experience Before You Die) which crosses the Wicklow Way.  The local roads are suitable for walking and cyclists and are within a couple of miles of the Military Road that leads to Glencree and on to The Sally Gap and Glendalough.  The Bohernabreena waterworks are within easy walking distance and the mountains are accessible within a short walk up a rural road.   There are many local attractions and places of historical interest within easy driving distance, including  Glencree,  Enniskerry  village and Powerscourt House and Gardens. notes: If walking and hiking please bring suitable gear, the weather in these hills is changeable. The drive and garden can get muddy, children may need wellies. Your fancy going-out footwear is better kept for city excursions!! Mobile phone reception can come and go in the space due to the hilly location. Also the wifi can occasionally be unreliable for the same reason. All part of the charm! We provide some basic food stuffs including tea, coffee, small amount of milk, jam, marmalade, honey, olive oil for cooking, salt, pepper and some spices. There are herbs growing outside including lemon balm, sage, thyme, parsley, majoram, mint & fennel. There have been a lot of visitors passing through lately and there may be oils, pasta and other non perishable foods that others have left, please make use of anything there. transit: We are not on a direct public transport route. We are 16.5km from Dublin City Centre.  Getting here will be easiest if you have your own mode of transport, which will be essential if you want to explore beyond the immediate walking and mountain trails. For walkers it is possible to take the public bus (49 or 75) as far as Oldbawn from where you can take a taxi from the Old Mill Pub (approx. €12 for a 10 minute drive).   For walkers on the Dublin Mountain Way which starts/ends at Sean Walsh Memorial Park in Tallaght It is about 2 hours walking to reach us. This is a popular route for hikers and cyclists, however the initial climb into the valley is steep so pace yourself. (It takes me about 40 minutes to cycle from Oldbawn – but I’m not super-fit). From Dublin airport we are about 40 minutes drive via the M50 motorway. The nearest shops/pub are at Oldbawn (10 minutes drive). Johnny Fox’s famous Dublin mountain pub and restaurant is about 30 minutes drive from here (across the mountains)

transit: The 16 bus from the airport stops nearly in front of the apartment. It's the cheapest way in but takes nearly an hour. neighborhood_overview: The lively and picturesque villages of Monkstown, Blackrock and Dalkey are within walking distance where you will find numerous cafes, restaurants and bars. All can be recommended without exception.  Enjoy long walks along the East & West Piers in Dún Laoghaire and the coastline. Literary lovers will enjoy the Joyce Tower in Sandycove where Ulysses is set and swimmers will relish the famous 40ft bathing area in front of the Martello Tower. Dún Laoghaire has many art galleries, a theatre and multiplex cinema. Within minutes of the house are three supermarkets, a chemist and a café as well as two great pubs, McCormack’s and Bakers Corner, that serve excellent food all day. And if you wish to go to the city, the 46A bus passes the house and will have you there in 20/30 minutes or take the train from Dún Laoghaire which travels to the city and also along the coastline towards Wicklow.
notes: Dún Laoghaire and the surrounding areas of Monkstown, Blackrock and Dalkey  are crowded with an array of great eating places and pubs. There are an abundance of amenities in the area and many websites to visit whether you are interested in literary history or the great outdoors. See our Guidebook for a comprehensive list of things to see and do in the immediate area and further afield.
transit: We are lucky to be on one of the main bus routes (46A) to Dublin city centre with a bus stop a few metres from the house or you could travel the coastline by train if you prefer, the nearest station a 20 minute walk away or an 8 minute bus ride. We provide guests with a Leap Card which gives up to 20% discount off public transport.  We have free off street parking for guests who are driving.  There are two car rental companies around the corner.  We are very close to the N11 & M50 motorway. Taxis are available 24/7 and can be hailed on the street or booked in advance.

space: This apartment sits at the top of a Georgian building. Bear in mind this means a lot of stairs to go up and no lift!! Over 100 years ago it housed the Irish government.   This is the building where rebels including Michael Collins and Eamon de Valera first established the Irish Republican Army with the purpose of freeing the Irish people from British rule. So with all this in mind, the apartment is not new and modern - it has some flaws!  I have decorated it in a vintage style with my own art and that of other local artists. Everything that you need to see in Dublin is also literally at your doorstep!!

Despite the excellent location, the area is very quiet and removed from the bustling nightlife districts of Dublin city centre. Furthermore, the area is very safe and the building is secure.

Dublin's main railway station (Heuston station) is within walking distance and the central bus station can be reached in 10 minutes by the Luas.

neighborhood_overview: Sandymount is one of the Dublin's best urban villages with the city centre just a stone's throw away. The area boasts a beautiful coastal promenade as well as a range of coffee shops, boutiques and restaurants, organic food stores, butchers, pubs, cricket grounds, bike shops & rental, a bookie shop, hairdressers, pharmacies and a supermarket. The Aviva stadium and RDS are both within short walks along with Bath Avenue & Merrion Road where you will find many popular Irish pubs for young and old. The Bord Gais Energy Theatre and Grand Canal Dock are both within a 20 minute walk or short taxi. The 3Arena (formerly 02 / Point Depot) is a 20 minute walk or short taxi. The Ballsbridge business / embassy district including the US embassy is within 2.4km of the house. Merrion Square and the National Gallery are 30 minute walks away whilst Stephen's Green and Grafton Street are a 40 minute walk away or 10 minute taxi.
transit: Public transport is on your doorstop. The DART (Dublin train service) is within 700 meters of the house. With this, you can travel out as far south as Bray & Greystones in Wicklow (passing by beautiful scenic and historical areas such as Dalkey & Killiney) and you can travel as far north as Malahide or stunning Howth Head (passing through central town on your way). The Bus stop is 2 minutes away and beside the Bus stop is a taxi rank. The Aircoach service from Dublin airport to Greystones (route 702) passes right by Sandymount (Get off at The Clayton Hotel Merrion Road stop). This runs on an hourly basis and costs €13 for a return trip. A taxi from the airport will cost you roughly €30.

neighborhood_overview: With major venues on our doorstep access to concerts, theatre and sporting events couldn't be easier. The Aviva, Shelborne Park, 3 Arena & Bord Gais Theatre at Grand Canal Square are betweeen 500m and 1km from the apartment. The RDS (along the river) and Convention Centre (via Point Village or Grand Canal Square) are both only 20 minutes walk. There's no need to worry about parking as there is a designated free space in the gated car park below the apartment complex - a rarity so close to the city. There is a supermarket and off-license, pharmacy, bistro and a number of local pubs around the corner. Other options for good quality food include Coppinger Row at Charlotte Quay, The Old Spot, Chop House, The Bath and Farmer Browns on Bath Avenue as well as Herb Street, The Marker Brasserie & Lolly & Cooks at Grand Canal Square which all are within 15 minutes walk.
notes: If you choose us rest assured that we are committed hosts. Our aim is to provide a fairly priced and high standard of accommodation with a personal touch. It's really important to us that you have a comfortable and enjoyable AirBnB experience that feels like home. The apartment is fully cleaned and serviced to a very high standard ready for your arrival. We provide clean towels and fresh bed linen for each of the guest as well as some toiletries, household laundry and essentials. We always leave something for you to eat when you arrive and for breakfast.
transit: The area is very well serviced by public transport and a car is not required for the city. There are two bus routes which provide direct access to the city in less than 10 minutes (1, 47). The buses which serve the airport - Airlink and Aircoach (702, 703) stop about 15 minutes walk away at the 3Arena.  Additionally both DART and Luas services are accessible within a few minutes walk of the apartment. Dublin Bikes (public bike rental scheme) are located at South Dock Road (approximately 2 minutes walk from the complex).
access: Guests enjoy private access to the apartment, recently upgraded high speed internet & WiFi, a designated free car parking space and use of the garden.  We appreciate that visitors may arrive early in the morning or late at night and are happy to fit in flexibly with your arrival time. Please let us know your plans when booking. Our normal check-out time is 11am however with prior arrangement it is usually possible to facilitate a later time if needed.
interaction: As soon as you book we'll send you links to useful information to help you plan your trip. About a week before you we'll provide you with instructions on how to find us. Please help us to provide you with the right information by telling us about your group, where you're travelling from and how you plan to get to us.  We like to personally greet our AirBnB guests to make sure everything is as you expect and show you how to work everything to ensure you get the most from you stay and it's trouble free. Although we stay off site we will text or email to make sure everything is working out and if help is needed we're available.  It's been our pleasure to meet business travellers, couples & lovely families and to contribute to making their trip to Ireland great.
house_rules: This listing is suitable for couples, families, mature groups and business travelers.  For your comfort the apartment has a maximum occupancy of 4 adults.  In order to maintain the high standard we ask guests to respect the furnishings and please note the sofa is not suitable for use as a bed. We ask that visitors respect residents of the complex by keeping noise to a minimum after 11pm, particularly if entering or leaving after this time. To help us best meet your needs please provide guest information and planned arrival / check out times as soon as possible after booking. WE may be able to facilitate early check in / out please check at time of booking.

Each day I had plans around the city so I was out and about after a quick cup of coffee and some toast. When I came home in the evening I had access to the kitchen to make a simple meal for myself, and then later I could hang out in my room and watch a movie on Netflix. That's the kind of place that I wanted to set up here.

Take Out food is always an option. But as an alternative, I keep some basic food available for my guests: tea, coffee, cereal, bread, jam, fruit, milk, and yummy Irish butter. Enough for a quick supper or breakfast the next morning before heading out for the day.

host_about:
I am a single mum and I love to spend time with my daughter and her friends. We love to play board games, be crafty and take long walks in St. Anne's Park or at the zoo. 

I first stayed in an Airbnb rental when I visited New York in the summer of 2015. I got a bedroom in an All Airbnb house, the host didn't live there, and it was perfect for me. Each day I had plans around the city so I was out and about after a quick cup of coffee and some toast. When I came home in the evening I had access to the kitchen to make a simple meal for myself, and then later I could hang out in my room and watch a movie on Netflix. One evening I shared a bottle of wine in the back garden with a few other guests from around the world. It was the perfect place to come home to after a crazy day of doing the tourist thing. That's the kind of place that I wanted to set up here.

Also, I know what it's like to arrive at a destination after a long day's travel, late in the day, tired and hungry, and hate to think about finding a shop to buy food.  Take Out food is always an option. But as an alternative, I keep some basic food available for my guests: tea, coffee, cereal, bread, jam, fruit, milk, and yummy Irish butter. Enough for a quick supper or breakfast the next morning before heading out for the day. 

I live just up the road from my Airbnb and I'm very hands on. I respond quickly to all questions from my guests. I have a lock box set up so that guests can check themselves in, but I like to know when my guests are due to arrive. That way I'm available to handle any issues that arise. I really enjoy helping my guests in any way that I can and over the past two years I've met so many wonderful people from all over the world, it's been super!

neighborhood_overview: South Lotts Road is an area of double storey terraced houses which were built between 1890 and 1910 to house the dockers working locally. The area was developed by James Beckett. The two storied dwellings are typically Red Bricked, two up, two down terraced houses with a small back yard.  The two up two down houses were built in the Belfast style with two rooms upstairs and two rooms downstairs. The houses have two upstairs windows and a single larger window downstairs overlooking the street. The facades are red bricked with blonde bricks around the door and windows. Each house originally contained a large fireplace in the front room downstairs and a smaller cast iron fireplace in the upstairs front and back rooms. Between the houses are older reclaimed bricks. Those bricks are believed to have been reclaimed from brick houses knocked down elsewhere in Dublin. The area has been used as a location in three major studio films, In the Name of the Father, The General and Education Rita.
notes: Hungry and Thirsty? If you're feeling hungry - you're in luck! There are 7 fantastic restaurants just down the street from our house. Go out the door, take a right and walk for 5 minutes to the intersection. Here you will find: The Chophouse - great for steak!  Paulie's Pizza - best pizza in town! The Old Spot - amazing burger (when they haven't run out)! Farmer Browns - one of the best brunch spots in Dublin! The Bath - great bar that also does a fab brunch at weekend - the ricotta hotcakes are soooo good!  Juniors - everything is great!  And if you fancy a good pint of Guinness - try Slattery's!

neighborhood_overview: A five minute walk through Ranelagh Gardens leads you to lively Ranelagh village, where you'll find great restaurants, bars, pubs, shops, and one of the best coffeeshops in the city. Nearby, Rathmines and Portobello also offer some great spots for breakfast, lunch, dinner and drinks! To get into the city centre a ten minute tram ride or a leisurely 20 minute stroll brings you to the Grafton Street area where all your shopping needs will be satisfied, and to get away from it all you can lose yourself in the leafy haven of St. Stephen's Green. Alternatively you can walk or rent a Dublin Bike and head down bustling Camden Street, onto Georges Street and into Temple Bar where you'll find cultural organisations, galleries, and theatres a-plenty, as well as a few not so jammed pubs and bars, and some great vintage and second hand clothing stores!
notes: We have a lovely cat, Yeta, who goes for wanders during the day but stays in at night. If inside during the day he likes to lounge about the house but sleeps in the kitchen at night. If you have an allergy or an aversion to cats, our place might not be the best for you. If you are renting the entire house we do book Yeta into a lovely local cat boarding accommodation so you don't have to worry about him being in the house during your stay!
transit: Ranelagh is easily reached from Dublin Airport via the Aircoach bus service, and the Leeson Street stop is only five minutes walk from the house. Alternatively there are a few city bus services which will get you to the house with one bus change along the way. A taxi is the easiest but most expensive option. Depending on availability, we can offer to pick you up from the airport and bring you back to the house for €20. Public transport options connecting Ranelagh to the city centre are the green Luas tramline, a couple of bus services, and the Dublin Bike rental scheme. More details can be provided once booking is confirmed.

summary: My two bedroom apartment is actually beside the Liffey with views out of every room of the famous Ha'penny bridge.  All the main tourist sites are only minutes walk away. space: You won't find anywhere more central Dublin without actually sleeping in Temple Bar square. Go downstairs, get a coffee and fresh-baked pastry from the Italian family coffee-shop, walk across the bridge and Temple Bar is at your feet. O'Connell St, Grafton St, Trinity College, National Gallery, Stephens Green, Dublin Castle, and the Guinness factory are all within a few minutes walk away. neighborhood_overview: Dublin is a small buzzing city with everything in walking distance. I think it rivals any European capital for tourist sites, pubs, food, history, music and general good fun. I live mainly overseas now but I love getting back and staying here as often as I can.  My place is right in the city centre, beside the river Liffey.  This means you're literally minutes from everything. My neighbours in the block are nice people, who are generally quiet and keep to themselves and I'd politely ask that you always keep the noise to a reasonable level and keep them happy with me. It's great sharing the Dublin experience with my guests and I hope to be able to keep doing it. thanks Kevin
notes: The apartment has a fully functional kitchen, with all the implements and pans etc needed to cook up home meals if you, or your wallet, want a break from Dublin's restaurant scene. Speaking of which, you should take a walk around George's St for a culinary tour of the planet. If you fancy something special and unusual, I'd recommend you make a reservation at the tapas bar at Fade St Social (if you can get a table). If it's an extra special occasion, try Chapter One up on Parnell Square, they win Ireland's best restaurant award on a regular basis. *We provide bed linen and towels.
transit: From Dublin airport the 747 express bus runs every 15 mins and takes about 30 mins(€6 single, €10 return). Easiest is to get off at O'Connell St stop, walk to the river and turn right before you cross and we're on the quays at the second footbridge. A taxi from the airport should cost about €30. If you're driving, there are 2 public car parks about 3 minutes walk away on Jervis St. Bikes are available for hire from a shop just along the river beside O'Connell Bridge. Taxis are everywhere. Dublin is small, so you'll probably find that you walk everywhere, but if you plan on using public transport a lot then it might be worth buying a "LEAP" travel card which you re-charge at newsagents and can be used on the buses, trams (Luas) and local trains (DART).
access: The apartment is on the first floor of a quiet, clean, well maintained, secure block with a lift. If you'd had enough sight-seeing, there is a private communal garden area, accessible outside the lift on the ground floor, with benches where you can sit outside with your book and enjoy the weather. If you're arriving early or checking out late, we'll do our best to accommodate you. But if it's not possible, there are coin-operated luggage lockers in the Jervis St shopping centre around the corner, where you can dump your bags while you go and explore Dublin.
interaction: Either I or my friend Gary will meet you, show you into the apartment and help you with local directions. If there's anything specific you want to see or do, during your stay, just tell us and we'll help you find it. Then we'll be on call to help you with any problems or question that you might have. Gary has lived in central Dublin for years and has lots of local knowledge.
house_rules: NO PARTY/STAG/HEN groups please. No loud noise in the block after 8pm. Please respect my neighbours. Note: Guests are advised to have their own personal insurance policy to cover accidents, injury or loss/damage to property. The host accepts no responsibility for any loss, damage or personal injury during their stay. In booking you agree to these terms and conditions.
host_about: Hi, I'm a Dublin native now living most of the year in Italy where I work as an independent consultant. But Dublin will always be my home too and I get back as often as I can.  This is a great block with good neighbours and right in the heart of everything. I love staying here myself and I like for others to experience it too. If you've never been to Dublin before, you're in for a great time.

host_about:
I'm a very curious woman, proud of being member of Couchsurfing. As such, I love travelling, eating, chatting and exploring. 
I can't live without music, food, good friends, love and travelling. 
I'm from Brazil. I've been to a couple of countries in South America and a few in Europe. My wishlist is still very long, though. 
I don't have a favorite travel destination, but, Paris and Gibraltar were pretty special...Morrocco is a place I'm looking forward to visiting. 

My favorites movies are the ones based on true stories or documentaries: Frida, The salt of the earth, the pianist etc.

My food is whatever is tasty...and includes meat!

I'm the kind of guest who likes sharing experiences and learn from the locals. This is what I love about Couchsurfing and is pretty much what I expect from Airbnb. I'm not fussy. I was looking for a place to stay in Gibraltar when I saw this 'B&B-boat' among the options. Guess which one I picked? Have you ever stayed in a boat? I have :D

My life motto is in Portuguese (my first language) and doesn't really make sense in English. I'll be more than happy to explain it to you if we ever meet each other.

neighborhood_overview: Christchurch Cathedral is about 2 blocks from Temple Bar and a literally minutes from all the other main Dublin attractions - Trinity college, Dublin Castle, Grafton St, O'Connell St, National Gallery etc etc. Turn left outside the front door, follow the crowd and you'll be enjoying a pint at the Guinness factory in no time.
notes: My block has an on-site caretaker to make sure its always well-maintained and secure. It's easy to find, being literally across the Christchurch cathedral and is perfectly positioned for exploring Dublin. The space itself is large for a one bed apartment, so you can put away all your luggage and the kitchen should have everything you need for easy self-catering.  We have super-fast wireless broadband and an internet TV, which you use to stream directly or cast from your phone or device. The sofa-bed is one of the best you can buy (please take care of it) and very comfortable.  Gary and myself will do our best to help you with early check-in or late departure, but where it's not possible there's an internet cafe with a bag storage service 50m away on Lord Edward St where you dump your stuff and go sight-see. We provide bed linen and towels.
transit: Jurys Hotel next door has a secure carpark accessed from Werburgh St. Getting a taxi to and from the apartment is easy from the rank outside the hotel door. Dublin's 747 airport bus stops at Parliament St. From there walk 100m towards the Cathedral and we're on the left-hand side between Sunny's newsagent and Jurys. Dublin is a small city, easily walkable to nearly everywhere.  If you fancy exploring further afield it might be worth buying a public transport LEAP card which you re-charge at newsagents and can be used on buses, local trains and trams.
access: My block has  a really cool roof terrace with views of Dublin city centre and the mountains that you'll struggle to find anywhere.  There are about a dozen benches in little secluded nooks and it's a great place to enjoy your book and  the weather.
interaction: When I'm in Ireland, I'm usually staying here myself so I don't often get to meet my guests face-to-face. But my friend Gary is my stand-in and he's a great host.  He will check you in, explain everything and help with any specific things you want to see or do in Dublin. He has loads of local knowledge to make sure you get the most out of your stay.
host_about: Although I now live mainly abroad, my family still love Dublin and are lucky enough to have this place to call home when we are here. We love the quiet secure building and the big sky views from the windows . We actually live most of our year in the countryside so to come here and have so many different shops and restaurants on our doorstep is a real treat for us. We hope you will enjoy all the things that Dublin has to offer too.

The area has strong links to Dublin's Viking past reflected in its colourful Nordic street names. The surrounding borough's of Smithfield, Cabra, Broadstone, Phibsborough and the Four Courts formed a key battleground during the Easter 1916 Rising, an event which led to the formation of the modern Irish state and is enjoying its centenary celebration this year.  This is a very friendly, welcoming neighbourhood with an eclectic mix of young and old living in the community. It is the perfect place to base yourself as a visitor, while at the same time getting a flavour for daily life in this energetic and exciting city. An institution in Dublin, it serves delicious, fresh fare and is a must-visit. Alongside the cafe is The Fumbally Stables, offering yoga classes, interesting workshops and events, and massage treatments for weary travellers. The Green Door Market nearby is also worth checking out.  You are also a 10 minute walk to Camden Street, Wexford Street, George’s Street, and Harcourt Street, full of cool Dublin nightlife.  The apartment is also convenient for sightseeing. The majestic St Patrick’s Cathedral is just by the apartment, and the Teeling Whiskey Distillery is only 5 minutes walk away. It is a short 10 minute bus journey or a 15 minute walk to Temple Bar, Trinity College Dublin and the Book of Kells. St Stephen’s Green is also a 15 minute walk, as is Grafton Street, the main shopping strip in Dublin.
transit: From the airport, the apartment is only a 30 minute drive or taxi journey. The journey to the apartment should cost about €20-30 by taxi. From the airport you can also catch the Aircoach (€12.00 return) or the 747 Airlink bus (€10.00 return). Both buses will drop you at Dame Street / Trinity College and from there it is a short bus or taxi ride to the apartment.  Dublin is well connected by buses and they are probably the most convenient way of going from A to B. You can buy a Leap card in most newsagents / convenience stores which you can top up with credit and then use on public transport throughout the city. Dublin also has 2 overground tram systems, the DART and the LUAS.  If the weather is good, Dublin Bikes are also great, with lots of stations dotted around the city. summary: This bright and spacious apartment is located in a Georgian house built in the 1790s and features high ceilings, huge windows and views of leafy Mountjoy Square. It's a five minute walk to historic O'Connell Street and the lively bustle of the city centre, with excellent public transport connections for the airport and for exploring more of Ireland. Come stay in the heart of Dublin and experience the everyday life of the city on your doorstep.
space: The apartment is located on the first floor of an old Georgian home, overlooking the greenery of Mountjoy Square Park. It most likely served as a drawing room when the house was first built and many of the original period features are still intact. The windows are floor-to-ceiling and south-facing, meaning the apartment is full of natural light throughout the day, even in winter. The open living space is perfect for lounging, reading and relaxing. There is a fully-equipped kitchen with a microwave, fridge, oven, kettle, toaster and complimentary tea and coffee. The bed is king-sized, the bathroom has an electric power shower and there is high-speed WiFi throughout the premises.

neighborhood_overview: Mountjoy Square is only a stone's throw away from Dublin's main sights, theatres, museums, galleries and parks. The apartment is located just a five minute walk to the top of historic O'Connell Street and the main shopping areas, restaurants and pubs are all within easy walking distance.   The area is also home to many working Dubliners and it's a great place to take in the ordinary life of the city. Just five minutes north of Mountjoy Square is Croke Park, the legendary home of Gaelic games and a hub of excitement and activity whenever there's a match on.
notes: Please note that there is no working elevator in the building, so the apartment may not be suitable for guests with mobility issues. There is no T.V. in this apartment. We will not be getting a T.V. at any stage. :) You're on you holidays
transit: Most of Dublin's major cultural attractions are within easy walking distance of the apartment, and the public transport links are also excellent. One of our favourite ways to get around the city centre is Dublin Bikes, a public bike service with stations located on Mountjoy Square. Leap Card is the quickest and easiest way to use public transport in Dublin. It works on Dublin Bus, the Luas and the DART. You can buy a Leap Card at the ticket machines in train stations and in many newsagents around the city.  The No. 7 and No. 8 buses stop just across the road from the apartment and will take you directly into the city centre. The No. 41 bus coming from the airport also stops on the Square. We are located a ten minute walk from Connolly Station and Busáras, which is handy if you're planning further travel in Ireland.

host_about:
Hi there 
I'm Irish, at least in part, though my mother is Swiss and my father
Turkish. I've lived in lots of great cities, like Berlin, Paris, New
York, and, of course, Dublin, which has its own very unique charm
that is much more dependent on the unpredictable weather and
constantly shifting light than you might think!

I like to travel, but what I like most is to stay in a place for
longer periods of time (to live there, in other words) and to get into the
language and culture as fully as possible.

Apart from that I'm a PhD student in literature and history of
science. I also love the cinema, weekend brunches (especially in
Dublin!), and being scandalised by the current state of the world!

As I am in NYC at the minute my pal Aoife will be managing things at my Dublin apartment. She knows Dublin well and will be able to give you plenty of advice :) 

All best,
Celia

The park leads to two neighbouroods Stoneybatter and Smithfield where there are a number of great coffee shops, places for brunch, traditional Irish bars with live music, cute shops and some other great bars and places to eat. neighborhood_overview: Rathgar is a quiet town in Dublin's Southside just 10-15 minutes away from the city centre by taxi or by bus with its very regular service. If you like walking, St Stephen's Green or George's Street is a bit over half an hour walk away. Rathgar is a residential area and has a great selection of local gourmet produce available in Super Valu and in The Butler's Pantry. The 108 Bar has an extensive local and international craft beer selection as well as a few rare whiskeys. The Bottlers Bank, just across the road, is more traditional, with original fittings and fantastic character.  Rathmines is a short walk down the road where there are bakeries, cafes, restaurants and a swimming pool. The Blackbird is a new pub for a younger crowd, with old beds being transformed into tables and an eclectic selection of board games. Mother Reilly's, locally known as Ma Reilly's, is a more traditional style, with most of its furniture and decor moved from an 18th century pub in Tipperary.

The location can't be beaten, with Dublin City Centre on your doorstep and Dublin's Business District nearby. If you plan to experience one of Dublin's legendary Rugby weekends Aviva Stadium and the RDS are a 5-10 minute taxi drive away, or if your trip is for work, the Dublin 2 Business District is a short stroll away, with Barrow Street, Silicone Dock, the IFSC, the National Convention Centre and the RDS all easily accessible.
notes: Each of our six stylishly decorated Double Rooms is uniquely decorated, and named after a famous local legend to reflect the house's fascinating history. If you need more than one Room, just let us know and we will do our best to accommodate you.
transit: Ranelagh Rooms is the perfect place from which to explore the City, either on foot or by public transport. The City Centre is just a short stroll away, and Charlemont Luas (Tram) Stop and the No 44 and 61 buses are on your doorstep. GoCar Members can pick up their Rental Car just across the road from the house at the Northbrook Road GoCar Pick Up Station, and the nearest Dublin Bike Station is one block away at the Charlemont Luas Stop. Dublin Airport is a 14km drive, and easily accessible by Taxi, Bus, Aircoach and the Airlink Express. There is FREE on-street parking at weekends and evenings (Pay & Display during the day Monday - Friday). Guests can find extensive detailed information on How to Find Us, Getting To and From the Airport, Parking, and Dublin Public Transport on the Ranelagh Rooms website.
access: After booking Guests will receive a personal Keycode that will give them access to the property for the duration of their stay. Guests can enter the Front Door and Luggage Store from 7am on Day Of Arrival until 10pm on Day of Departure, and the Patrick Kavanagh Room from Check-in time of 3pm on Day of Arrival until Check-out time of 12pm on Day of Departure.
interaction: We use Smartlocks so that Guests can Check-in and Check-out at a time that suits them. neighborhood_overview: Merrion Square has an abundance of strengths from its strong Georgian heritage, cultural institutions, leisure facilities, and its political, social and scientific history. Mapped out 250 years ago in 1762, it has fine Georgian Houses on three sides and the garden of Leinster House and The National Gallery and Natural History Museum on the 4th. Oscar Wilde lived as a child at 1 Merrion Square, where Bram Stoker also spent a lot of time attending Lady Wilde’s salons, while W. B. Yeats lived at No 82, and Daniel O’Connell at No 58. The Square is well known for its Sunday Open Art Gallery and is home to  the Irish Traditional Music Archive, the Irish Architectural Archive, the Irish Georgian Society, the Society of Antiquarians.  It has a stunning public park at the centre of the Square which provides an appealing and relaxing atmosphere for locals and visitors alike, and now has a mobile café operated by Tir na nOg called “Coffee in the Park” situated near the East entrance.

neighborhood_overview: If I wasn’t from there, Howth peninsula in north county Dublin would be on my bucket list of places to visit in Ireland. For generations it has witnessed many Irish marriage proposals on its beautiful cliffs! A stone’s throw from Dublin city but a holiday destination in its own right, Howth is a looped peninsula with stunning vistas out onto Lambay island, Slieve Gullion and the Mourne Mountains. Take one of the interestingly named circular walks (black linn, bog of frogs, cliff path and tramline loop) and in addition to the stunning scenery you may encounter kittiwakes, guillemots, razorbills and grey seals. Take a break in the Summit Inn or finish your walk with well-deserved refreshments in the Bloody Stream (a pub that is built into the old railway station and is named after the blood that was spilled in the Norman defeat of the Vikings at Howth in the 12th century). There is also a night-link bus service from Dublin city centre on Friday and Saturday nights. It goes from midnight to 4am on the hour and costs about €6. It goes over Howth Summit so it’s advisable not to have too many pints of the black stuff!

neighborhood_overview: Rathgar is a quiet town in Dublin's Southside just 10 minutes away from the city centre by taxi or by bus with a very regular service. If you like walking, St Stephen's Green or George's Street is a bit over half an hour away. Rathgar has a great selection of local gourmet produce available in Super Valu and in The Butler's Pantry. The 108 Bar has an extensive local and international craft beer selection as well as a few rare whiskeys. The Bottlers Bank, just across the road, is more traditional, with original fittings and fantastic character.  Rathmines is a short walk down the road where there are bakeries, cafes, restaurants and a public swimming pool. The Blackbird was once considered a pub for an older generation, it now caters a younger crowd, with old beds being transformed into tables and an eclectic selection of board games. Mother Reilly's, known locally as Ma Reilly's, is a more traditional style, with most of its furniture and decor moved from an 18th century pub in Tippera

Hugs

If you book with me I hope you can feel that joy.

A few minutes walk and you are gazing up at the magnificent Christchurch Cathedral. Large sections of the old medieval walls of Dublin remain in the neighbourhood, the area is steeped in history. transit: Because of it’s location, you will probably spend most of your time here travelling on foot.  However, for the weary traveller, taxis can be hailed on the street or you can use your Uber or Hailo app to order one to the door. A taxi to or from the airport will cost you €25-35, depending on traffic. The most common form of airport transport is bus, and you can catch the 747 Airlink Express or the Aircoach from College Green. A return airport fare is €10 and can be purchased on the bus or online.  Dublin is also serviced by a good bus network. You can buy a ‘leap card’ in many of the local shops and use this for a reduced fare to ‘tap on/off’. The buses that will take you to and from town are the 27A, the 56, the 77A, the 150 and the 151.  There are also public bicycles - Dublin Bikes - and a great, cheap way to travel around as a 3-day pass is only €5. The first half hour is free.

We like to collect art and antiques and dabble in a bit of furniture restoration and renovation.

We used to go out frequently but are now older (maybe not wiser) and spend time now on other pursuits - walking, furniture restoration, traveling, playing bridge (is that sad?!).

Life motto?  So many.... 

Live for the day
Seize the moment
One mans rubbish is another mans treasure  (I like to recycle!)
Fathers name family motto: ‘I Rise Through Difficulties’
Why lie awake thinking about it; just get up and do it!
So many mottos, so little time!  ;-)

neighborhood_overview: Skerries is a picturesque fishing village on the north coast of Dublin County. We have a local surf company that rents SUP boards and kayaks. There are (seasonal) boat trips available to Rockabill/Lambay Islands. We have a little Tourist office on Thomas Hand St. that can help you organise tours of the area. There are plenty of nice short, flat walks. The Mill offers a short tour and also has a gift shop and cafe. Ardgillan castle is only 10 minutes drive or 20 mins walk (via Ladies Stairs) walk away.  Skerries has many great award winning restaurants. Some of our favourites are Stoop Your Head, 5 Rock, Seasons, Olive and The 54. There are traditional music sessions in Joe Mays on a Sunday night and in the Snug on Thursday nights, Folk music in Nealons on Wednesdays and various bands in Raffs on Saturday nights.

neighborhood_overview: Rathgar is a quiet town in Dublin's Southside just 10 minutes away from the city centre by taxi or bus with a very regular service. If you like walking, St Stephen's Green or George's Street is a bit over half an hour away. Rathgar has a great selection of local gourmet produce available in Super Valu and in The Butler's Pantry. The 108 Bar has an extensive local and international craft beer selection as well as a few rare whiskeys. The Bottlers Bank is more traditional, with original fittings and fantastic character. Both pubs are a few mins walk from the apartment. Rathmines is a short walk down the road where there are bakeries, cafes, restaurants and a swimming pool. The Blackbird is a new pub for a younger crowd, with old beds being transformed into tables and an eclectic selection of board games. Rody Bolanes has a more traditional style, with most of its furniture and decor moved from an authentic 18th century pub in Tipperary.

neighborhood_overview: My neighbourhood is where the origins of the historical Dublin City began. Christchurch the largest Catholic Cathedral in town was built upon the original Viking settlements where Dublin City originated.  A trip to 'Dublinia' maps out how the City was during Viking times and their influence to this day.  Ironically at the bottom of St Patricks Street you will find St Patricks Cathedral, our other beautiful Cathedral looked over by the writer Dead Swift who was Dean of the Cathedral during the 1700's. Here you can take a walk in the adjoining park and have a coffee in it's pop up coffee shops.  A short distance from here is Grafton Street our main commercial high end shopping street. The amazing thing about Dublin is that you can walk everywhere, its large enough to have everything a city needs but small enough for it all to be fabulously accessible by foot, if you like walking.

You can stroll to the centre or take the LUAS tram or a bus if you don't fancy the walk - both of which are very close to the cottage. Stoneybatter has plenty of great spots to hang out in, whether you fancy a pint of Guinness in a traditional put, a cocktail, or a great coffee. To be honest, that’s only about 7 mins walk from the centre so it might not feel worth it to you. There are Dublin Bikes depots at Blackhall Place and at the north and south of Smithfield Square where the Lighthouse Cinema is. neighborhood_overview: Inchicore Village is a 3 minutes’ walk away and benefits from a host of shops and services that include a great local Italian restaurant (Enoteca Torino) and a friendly pub (the Black Lion) with live music and great Guinness. Visit the recently refurbished Richmond Barracks museum which held up to 3000 prisoners following the Easter Rising of 1916. The historical area of Kilmainham is only 15-20 min walk away with Kilmainham Gaol -Dublins most popular visitor attraction and IMMA Royal Hospital which includes beautiful  formal gardens. The War Memorial Park is also a short walk away with fountains, rose gardens and a stroll by the river Liffey.  The Phoenix Park- Europe's largest walled park-is close by and houses Dublin Zoo.

There is a good bus service to the city center taking in the Guinness Hopstore, Dublin Castle, Christchurch Cathedral and Trinity College. Dublin City bike station is 15 mins by foot from the house (at the Kilmaingham Gail). Bike rent for 3 days is only €5.

neighborhood_overview: The apartment is located on a quiet residential cobblestone street, but around the corner is the heart of a real Dublin city-center neighborhood.  There are several grocery stores nearby and tons of bars, restaurants and fast-casual dining options for food on the go. There is also a great hotel just around the corner if you fancy something a little more formal.  The IFSC/Docklands area is 5 mins walk away - in particular the CHQ building has many bars and restaurants, plus a great museum about Ireland.  From a cultural perspective The Abbey Theatre (Irelands National Theatre) is 5 mins away, Croke Park (80,000 seater Gaelic games stadium) is 15 mins walk, the 3 Arena (large indoor concert venue) is a 20 min walk / 5 mins on LUAS, and the Bord Gáis Theatre (large show/theatre venue) is 15 mins walk.  Plus the rest of the city is no more then 15 mins walk too!
notes: If you need parking, let me know in advance and I will arrange this.  We can sometimes (subject to availability) accommodate a late checkout or hold your luggage if you have a late flight - please ask in advance.  Similarly, sometimes an early check-in is available, subject to availability.
transit: Location is very central to all transport links and perfectly suited for a tourist.  • Airlink Express 747 airport shuttle bus has a dropoff stop 1 min walk from apartment.  • Connolly Rail Station is 2 mins walk. (Connolly is a major rail station with intercity links to the Northern half of Ireland and commuter and DART services across the city) • Busarus bus station is 2 mins walk. Busarus is Dublins main bus station with bus services across Ireland.  • LUAS is Dublins tram service which cross-crosses the city. The RED line stop at Busarus is 2 mins away. The GREEN line is 5 mins walk away.  • The tourist hop-on hop-off buses have their main start/end point in O Connell St, which is about 6 mins walk.  • Finally, the tour operators who go to Giants Causeway, Cliffs of Moher etc usually originate from O Connell St which is about 6 mins walk.
access: Guests will have full use of the bedroom and sole use of the full bathroom. Limited access to the kitchen is permitted (ie to use the fridge etc) though we prefer to keep this space mostly private.
interaction: We are generally available to answer any questions or queries from guests, and we include a broad range of maps and tourist brochures in the room for your perusal. I really enjoy helping my guests in any way that I can and over the past two years I've met so many wonderful people from all over the world, it's been super!

With its back to the sea and its front to the incredible green square you can picnic and swim literally on your doorstep. Across the park is the famous Cultulann (the Irish cultural institute) where you can play or learn traditional Irish music by a lot fire drinking a fresh pint of stout. In Monkstown village, just 10 minutes walk away, you can savour some of the finest food in Dublin. If you want access to Dublin City you've come to the right place. host_about:
CURRENT MISSION

Live the life now, check the world and have as much fun as I can.

ABOUT ME

A friendly funny guy, not too noisy, not too quiet. Always ready for a beer or to help with a puncture!

PHILOSOPHY

Live as the hummingbird story-

One day a terrible fire broke out in a forest - a huge woodlands was suddenly engulfed by a raging wild fire. Frightened, all the animals fled their homes and ran out of the forest. 
As they came to the edge of a stream they stopped to watch the fire and they were feeling very discouraged and powerless. They were all bemoaning the destruction of their homes. 
Every one of them thought there was nothing they could do about the fire, except for one little hummingbird. This particular hummingbird decided it would do something. It swooped into the stream and picked up a few drops of water and went into the forest and put them on the fire. Then it went back to the stream and did it again, and it kept going back, again and again and again. 
All the other animals watched in disbelief; some tried to discourage the hummingbird with comments like, "Don't bother, it is too much, you are too little, your wings will burn, your beak is too tiny, it’s only a drop, you can't put out this fire." 
And as the animals stood around disparaging the little bird’s efforts, the bird noticed how hopeless and forlorn they looked. Then one of the animals shouted out and challenged the hummingbird in a mocking voice, "What do you think you are doing?" And the hummingbird, without wasting time or losing a beat, looked back and said, "I am doing what I can."

Why to use bnb

Travel is one of my loves in life, and I think that AirBnB is one of the best options to do it. For me a trip is not to travel somewhere and take some pictures. I want to know people, do the things people do where I travel and learn another ways of life!!

Interests

Live music, go out for a beer, enjoy a good meal and spend as much time as I can with my friends! 
I'm trying to learn how to play the guitar but I just manage to play some songs.. anyway it's cool that way!

neighborhood_overview: The house is in the Liberties which is one of Dublin’s oldest and fascinating areas which is a short walking distance to many historical attractions such as Christchurch Cathedral, Teelings Whiskey Distillery, Jameson Distillery, Guinness Storehouse, St. Patricks Cathedral and Kilmainham Gaol. There are also many café’s, restaurants and bars around the area as well as the house being located just off Francis Street which is known as Dublin’s main Antique street. Meath Street is at the other end of my street which is home to the famous Liberty Market (Thursday-Saturday) and many shops and eateries. There is also a flea market which takes place in Newmarket Square on the last Sunday of every month and this would take approximately 5 minutes to reach by foot. This area is very popular with tourists considering its history and how centrally located it is, it really is a perfect location if you are looking to visit and experience all of what this great city has to offer.

host_about:
CURRENT MISSION

Live the life now, check the world and have as much fun as I can.

ABOUT ME

A friendly funny guy, not too noisy, not too quiet. Always ready for a beer or to help with a puncture!

PHILOSOPHY

Live as the hummingbird story-

One day a terrible fire broke out in a forest - a huge woodlands was suddenly engulfed by a raging wild fire. Frightened, all the animals fled their homes and ran out of the forest. 
As they came to the edge of a stream they stopped to watch the fire and they were feeling very discouraged and powerless. They were all bemoaning the destruction of their homes. 
Every one of them thought there was nothing they could do about the fire, except for one little hummingbird. This particular hummingbird decided it would do something. It swooped into the stream and picked up a few drops of water and went into the forest and put them on the fire. Then it went back to the stream and did it again, and it kept going back, again and again and again. 
All the other animals watched in disbelief; some tried to discourage the hummingbird with comments like, "Don't bother, it is too much, you are too little, your wings will burn, your beak is too tiny, it’s only a drop, you can't put out this fire." 
And as the animals stood around disparaging the little bird’s efforts, the bird noticed how hopeless and forlorn they looked. Then one of the animals shouted out and challenged the hummingbird in a mocking voice, "What do you think you are doing?" And the hummingbird, without wasting time or losing a beat, looked back and said, "I am doing what I can."

Why to use bnb

Travel is one of my loves in life, and I think that AirBnB is one of the best options to do it. For me a trip is not to travel somewhere and take some pictures. I want to know people, do the things people do where I travel and learn another ways of life!!

Interests

Live music, go out for a beer, enjoy a good meal and spend as much time as I can with my friends! 
I'm trying to learn how to play the guitar but I just manage to play some songs.. anyway it's cool that way!

host_about: Hello there! Ladies and gentlemen we are floating in space. My favourite band ever is 'Faith No More': I love their eclectic sound, they have recorded four phenomenal albums, but most of all I appreciate their sense of humour, especially about the serious things. My top two destinations that I have not yet been to are Cambodia and Antartica. I like to play chess, it's a way of dealing with infinity. I like to play football and swim. The life motto I repeat the most is, "Never be ashamed of what you don't know!", we all walk a different path in this life. My greatest weakness is talking about myself. As a guest I am not fussy: a hot shower, a comfortable place to lay my head and a roof are all I require. If you would like to discuss anything at all over a pint of beer, I will oblige. summary: If you are looking for a unique experience in Dalkey, this small but beautiful Architect designed loft style studio is for you. It is located behind a secret door on a small picturesque avenue located in only five minutes’ walk to the village with all its bars restaurants and amenities and in the other direction to Coliemore Harbour with its stunning views over Dalkey Island.
space: The space takes inspiration from the Mediterranean and is white throughout with a tiny stone sided courtyard outside.  The interior is decorated with beautiful prints and has stylish lighting throughout. You will have full cooking facilities- a four hob cooker, extractor, a washer dryer, a small TV, wi-fi and a music center. The loft space is accessed by quirky steps like those in a ships cabin, and has a cosy double bed from which you can catch glimpses of the sea.  A comgortable pull out couchbed can sleep additional guests and an additional matress is available if required. The shower is stylishly designed with glazed 'metro' style wall tiles. The space is highly insulated and is heated by an electric heater so you will be warm and comfortable no matter what the weather outside brings.

neighborhood_overview: Dalkey, is a beautiful little medieval seaside town. While only 25 minutes by train to Dublin it has a strong local character and identity. It is a picturesque place -full of fine places to eat and drink. Located close by are beautiful coastal walks – stroll down to Coliemore Harbour and take a ferry to the island or  walk or around Killiney Hill taking in breath-taking views over Bray and Wicklow. If you feeling brave take a swim at White Rock Beach !
notes: The studio is located on a narrow avenue and our guests have found it tricky to reverse cars up the lane. They have all found it better to drop off and to use the free on street parking on Rockfort Avenue and to walk around-its only a 4 minute walk away !
transit: All transport links are within a short walk. The studio is about 5 minutes’ walk from the Dart station which will bring you directly into Dublin City Centre – a journey of about 25 minutes.  The Aercoach bus service to Dublin airport is approximately 10 minutes’ walk and is beside a local taxi rank.
access: The place has a tiny stone sided courtyard outside for you to enjoy. It is fully independent of the main house so you can come and go with ease.
interaction: Having grown up in the area I am always delighted to meet  with guests and to share local information particularly about where to eat, drink and all the spectacular local walks.
house_rules: Nothing too heavy !!!! - Its a super quiet neighbourhood and we always want our neighbours to feel comfortable so please be respectful !    No access to the flat roof except for emergency exit- this is to respect our neighbours privacy Thanks!!

host_about:
CURRENT MISSION

Live the life now, check the world and have as much fun as I can.

ABOUT ME

A friendly funny guy, not too noisy, not too quiet. Always ready for a beer or to help with a puncture!

PHILOSOPHY

Live as the hummingbird story-

One day a terrible fire broke out in a forest - a huge woodlands was suddenly engulfed by a raging wild fire. Frightened, all the animals fled their homes and ran out of the forest. 
As they came to the edge of a stream they stopped to watch the fire and they were feeling very discouraged and powerless. They were all bemoaning the destruction of their homes. 
Every one of them thought there was nothing they could do about the fire, except for one little hummingbird. This particular hummingbird decided it would do something. It swooped into the stream and picked up a few drops of water and went into the forest and put them on the fire. Then it went back to the stream and did it again, and it kept going back, again and again and again. 
All the other animals watched in disbelief; some tried to discourage the hummingbird with comments like, "Don't bother, it is too much, you are too little, your wings will burn, your beak is too tiny, it’s only a drop, you can't put out this fire." 
And as the animals stood around disparaging the little bird’s efforts, the bird noticed how hopeless and forlorn they looked. Then one of the animals shouted out and challenged the hummingbird in a mocking voice, "What do you think you are doing?" And the hummingbird, without wasting time or losing a beat, looked back and said, "I am doing what I can."

Why to use bnb

Travel is one of my loves in life, and I think that AirBnB is one of the best options to do it. For me a trip is not to travel somewhere and take some pictures. I want to know people, do the things people do where I travel and learn another ways of life!!

Interests

Live music, go out for a beer, enjoy a good meal and spend as much time as I can with my friends! 
I'm trying to learn how to play the guitar but I just manage to play some songs.. anyway it's cool that way!

host_about:
Hey Guys! 

My name is Tara and I'm from Malahide,Dublin. I live with my husband and our 6 year old daughter Annabelle. 

I've lived in Malahide all my life, as has both my parents. My Dad grew up in Malahide village and my Mom grew up in the cottage! The cottage has been passed down throughout our family for hundreds of years. I was recently been told by a local architect that it's as old as Malahide Castle!!

We're a foodie family so we know all the great local spots. Just let me know what cuisine or ambience you're looking for and we'd be happy to point you in the right direction.

I run a local Bootcamp for women so I also know the good spots for those looking for a healthy bite that tastes good. 

We did plenty of partying in our younger days so we can also point you in the right direction if you're looking for a fun night out :) :)

We love taking Annabelle for a kiddies babychino in Avoca after a trip to the playground in Malahide Castle. She's also a HUGE fan of their pancakes and cookies! The local play centre is owned by friends of ours and is a fantastic place to take the kids on a rainy day. They've got the adults covered with an onsite Cafe too!


I'm so excited to join Airbnb and I'm really looking forward to welcoming you to Malahide. 

See you soon! 

Tara, Stephen & Annabelle x

neighborhood_overview: The neighbourhood is the hippest  in Dublin with lots of boutique restaurants and funky bars  and is very cool, full of character with cobblestone streets and close to everything. Everything happens here! There's also a cinema, gyms, supermarkets right on the Square. Jameson distillery is in the complex. Recommend Proper Order on Haymarket St- the BEST coffee. For food; great breakfast at Third Space and Oscars'. For dinner Wuff and The Fish Shop both on Benburb Street are fantastic.  Craic; Cobblestones trad music bar is a classic, Frank Ryans bar and Dice bar all on the square are awesome as is The Glimmerman pub in nearby Stoneybatter which is a short walk away. You can walk over the liffey to the Brazen Head oldest pub in Ireland (Guinness stew is excellent here) and opposite it O Shea's merchant bar where you can ceili dance - great fun!
notes: Grab a bike (Dublin bikes on the Square) and cycle to Phoenix Park, an Airbnb World heritage pick. Sit outside and snack at the Victorian tea rooms and listen to the roar of the lions from neighbouring Dublin Zoo. Rustle up a meal in our well equipped kitchen, grab a beer and dine al fresco on the sun trapped balcony.
transit: Everything is within walking distance. Well serviced by buses and Dublin airport bus is a stroll away. Feeling lazy?...Grab any of  the tourist hop on hop off buses, they all go through the square. Temple bar is 8 minutes on foot from my place. O Connell street is 11 minutes away.
access: The whole space is yours. Also included secure underground car parking  in the apartment complex. I provide discount tickets for tourist attractions, city maps and a locals guide to all the cool awesome stuff to do and see in the city.. Also kids toys and games, good for adults too!!
interaction: Yes available to offer any help during your stay. What sets us apart is the personal touch, this is my home for a long time, not a rental and is furnished to a high standard (I feel). I love my fun city and love sharing all the special, local and different  things about it with guests so they can maximize their stay.  I travel widely and am sensitive to guests requirements and needs and want to make them happy.  We will be at the rental upon your arrival to give you a Big Irish Welcome! and provide you with a list of all the top tips; best pubs, restaurants and places to visit depending on your tastes and interests.  Available to answer questions and help make your stay super enjoyable

neighborhood_overview: Grand Canal Dock - also known as Dublin’s Tech Capital - is a bustling area where many well-known companies hold their headquarters. It is a modern neighbourhood, with great access to transportation, great restaurants/bars, and great urban design. It is a very pleasant 10-minute walk away from the IFSC, and only a 15-minutes walk away from Temple Bar and St. Stephen’s Green. Right across the canal from the apartment, you will also have very quick and easy access to Dublin’s Convention Centre. The Airlink 747 runs to and from the Convention Centre (approx. a 5 minute walk away from the apartment) from the Dublin Airport, therefore getting to the apartment is very easy. Alternatively, there are many taxis which can be hailed on the street or ordered via your Uber or MyTaxi app. A taxi to or from the Airport can cost between €30-35, depending on traffic. If you rather not walk too much around the city, a Leap card allows you to get on and off public transport with ease, and can be purchased at most local shops.

neighborhood_overview: Grand Canal Dock in central Dublin is home to the Bord Gais Energy Theatre, The Marker Hotel (5 Star), Surfdock Watersports, Barges, great restaurants and a lovely pub (The Ferryman). It is a very cosmopolitan area as people come from all over the world to work and live in it's lovely surroundings. Even Airbnb has offices in the area, which has been dubbed Silicon Dock. In the warm summer weather (we hope!) it's a great place to sit with a coffee or a beer and watch the world go by.
notes: During the summer there are frequent festivals on Grand Canal Square and the Liffey at the end of the road is often visited by beautiful Tall Ships.
transit: Directions from Dublin Airport The best way to get here from Dublin Airport is to get an Aircoach, just outside the terminal. You will be getting route No 702 that goes to Greystones. It costs €7 for a single adult or €12 for a return trip (worthwhile) You can book and pay online before you go, just search for the Aircoach website. You will also find the timetable online. Oh, and there's free wi fi on the coach.     Get off the coach at the Clayton Hotel at Grand Canal Dock. The apartment is about 2 blocks away - a very short walk.  There is a taxi rank just around the corner and the apartment is very near numerous public transport stops: Dart - Dublin Area Rapid Transport. Several bus routes, Dublin Bikes. City Tour buses stop around the corner Dublin Bay Cruises run from their Liffey base at the end of the road.
access: Guests will have the apartment entirely to themselves except for one small, locked room which I use for storage.
interaction: I may not always be available in person but, if not, I will leave you in the expert care of one of the friendliest, most capable people I know. Aoife will look after you during your stay and you will feel all the better for having met her.
host_about: I teach creative writing and so you won't be short of reading materials if you stay in my apartment! I love to travel but, in the end, Dublin is where I belong. I won't always be there to show you around but Aoife is the friendliest, most helpful person you've ever met. Believe me.

Whilst well within walking distance of most attractions, the area is generally more suited to younger travellers or people who are comfortable in diverse, city crowds, populated by people of all classes and creeds. Being so close to the major train station and many working class pubs, you may occasionally see some quite  intoxicated locals, but they are just on their own journey and keep to themselves. Some guests have reported feeling a bit unsafe at night, yet to this day, we have hosted over 15000 travellers without a single report of harm ever occurring. This can be validated by reading our 2400+ reviews. You won't find a single incident.
notes: - All linen, bedding towels etc are provided, and professionally laundered by Premier Linen Services. All of our apartments cleanliness and hygiene are looked after by a professional cleaning company that looks after over 100 apartments. Should you find any issues, please notify us as soon as convenient and we will have any issue rectified asap. - All the information you will need to use and enjoy our home is contained in our Home Manual, which will be send after payment is made and confirmed. Codes for security key boxes will be forwarded within 24-48 hours of check in.
transit: Close to every attraction. Walk.. Everywhere! Take a train or tram from across the road at Connolly Station, or take a tour bus, only five minutes walk away! Parking at Connolly Station, 5 mins walk, €15/24hrs.
