Because it is a holiday apartment letting, you get the keys and use it just like a holiday home. We also provide fast broadband along with a great recommendations guide, and for all other info we recommend checking out other travellers experiences via TripAdvisor. This will get you the best, most up to date info, instantly!

Jen

But also, consider some of the local hidden gems like Marsh's Library, The State Apartments in Dublin Castle or browse the Antique shops on Francis Street. neighborhood_overview: This is the historical part of Dublin, so you will be spoiled for choice. Dublinia is beside Christchurch and is a historical recreation museum, concentrating on Viking and medieval history of the city.  The Guinness Storehouse is well worth a visit.  Dublin Castle is 5 mins away, built in the 13th century.  Of course, Trinity College, Temple Bar, and the shopping area of Grafton Street are just a 10 to 15 minute stroll down through Dame Street passing the Olympia Theatre as you go.  Self hire Dublin bikes are available at Wood Quay, Christchurch Place, should you like to tour Dublin by bike.  In that case I would recommend a ride up to the Phoenix Park, one of the largest Public Parks in Europe and so beautiful, you might catch sight of a deer or a stag.  The Phoenix Park is about a 20 minutes walk, and if you like to get a run in on your break, you would certainly enjoy the sights here.
notes: All access to the apartment building is via secure electronic gates and doors from Nicholas Street.  I will supply two Electronic fobs and keys per booking.  These must be returned at the end of your reservation or there will be a lost fee of €60 each. The Samsung Washer/Dryer is a european size.  The washing machine door has a automatic lock mechanism which will not allow the door to be opened for 3 minutes after a wash has completed.  Please wait for the signal to unlock the door otherwise you will break the door handle.  It washes first and then there is a dry cycle.  The dry cycle dries a modest amount of clothes, like a few shirts, slips, socks at a time, not like an American dryer or washing machine, it won't be able to take a family load at once.  My sheets and towels are taken out and laundered, I do not wash them at the apartment for this reason.
transit: The Aircoach bus service to and from Dublin Airport stops at College Street outside Trinity. From here you can walk to Christchurch View in 10 minutes or take the 123 bus from across the road on the corner of College Green and Suffolk Street. A single ticket on the Aircoach costs €7.00 from the airport to Trinity. A taxi from the airport will take a good 25 minutes, pending traffic and set you back €25.00 to €30. Bus routes 123, bus 49, 77, 54  and 78 all stop near Christ Church. There are self hire bikes at Christ Church Place. There's no parking provided.  The nearest parking garage is Q-Park, Werburgh Street, Dublin 8, just a few minutes walk from the apartment.  It is cheaper to book on line, select Dublin Q-Park Christ Church

host_about:
Hello! Why does the idea of talking about oneself strike fear in one's heart, is it that we're just too bashful or the subject matter might be boring, ha.  I'm a mother of two young adults, a son whose taking the scenic route through life and a daughter who is kicking and screaming through a science degree, which automatically makes me a human ATM machine.  To survive motherhood I took up running some years ago and have ran many International Marathons including some of the majors New York, Boston, London, Paris, San Francisco all of which I qualified for where necessary.  I'm a glass half full type of person and certainly believe that if plan A doesn't work, there's always plan B, C, etc.,.  I enjoy meeting people and hosting with Airbnb has been a terrific experience for me in that regard.  In general I love to see people enjoying life and if I can help them in that goal, all the better.  I'm a believer in karma and thus each day is an opportunity to do something good and make people happy.  Of course , I have a huge work ethic and I like to give a 100% to whatever I'm working on.  I'm a  cleanliness freak, having had a bad experience in what I thought was a good hotel in London, long story short, I jumped into bed after a long day in London and a late theatre night, in the morning when I woke, I noticed there was a brown coffee stain on my sheet, obviously the sheets had not been changed, I was Not a happy camper!  Who would have thought, needless to say, I check wherever I stay now!   
I love Dublin city and the people, I'm a Dubliner even though my Dad hailed from County Kerry (the California of Ireland), and my Mum from County Westmeath.  I love to pretend to be a tourist in my own city, the things you notice and discover, always something new.  Life always has moments to be recorded, thus the advent of phones with cameras has enabled me to embrace my other passion, photography, I think I have at least 20,000 photos,  thank goodness for iCloud.
Hope all that didn't bore you too much, have a wonderful day, Namaste.:-)

summary: Experience luxurious camping conveniently located within walking distance of what Dublin city has to offer. notes: The neighborhood is pretty quite, but if you’re truly looking for peace and quiet, this might not be the place for you as we are in the city so you can expect a certain level of noise. It’s also worth mentioning that Dublin City Tipi is adjacent to a railway line so expect the occasional train passing which in fact might the highlight of your stay if you are lucky enough to experience a steam train passing up close! You are not going to have the tranquility of camping in the middle of nowhere. neighborhood_overview: Temple Bar is the essential area of Dublin. It is a beautiful pedestrian area with multiple streets filled with cafes, restaurants, pubs and interesting shops. In Temple Bar, you will never be stuck for choice, as everything is at your doorstep and it is a great place to taste our locally brewed beer, Guinness.    Within a 5 minute walk from the property is Trinity College Dublin, a historic georgian styled constituent and the home to the Book of Kells. Located directly beside Trinity college is our famous shop street, Grafton Street. Get a feel for Irish fashion and savour some great performances from buskers that fill the street with tranquil vibrations.    Also within walking distance (or a short bus ride if you prefer) from the property is O’Connell Street, 3Arena Stadium, the Bord Gais Energy Theatre and the Guinness Storehouse. The storehouse was voted one of europe's greatest tourist attractions.

The journey will take approximately 30-40 minutes and depending on traffic the journey will costs between €20 - €30.    If you would prefer using public transport, I would recommend catching the 747 Airlink Bus from the airport to the College Green stop; a return trip only costs €10. The property is only a 10 minute walk from this stop.   Another great way to get around the city is cycling. Located outside the property is a Dublin Bike Station. These stations are dotted around the city and offers a 3-day pass for €5.    If you wish to pop out of the city, you can do day trips to other cities and towns in the West and South of Ireland such as Westport, Galway and Cork. There is a train station called Tara Street Station that is only a 10 minute walk from the property.

Depending on availability, we can offer to pick you up from the airport and bring you back to the house for €20. The word Puck’s is an English mispronunciation of the Irish word “púca” or “pooka” (meaning ghost or spirit), so of course, the ruins are said to be haunted. Please, please do keep in mind that this is a hillside property, so even though all the famous online map and GPS services *say* that the bus routes are a "28 minute walk" (yeah, right!) I wouldn't dare suggest that you plan to walk to and from the local bus or rail services. Walking down on a fine day is nice, but walking back up the hill after a day of sight-seeing is just not a good option (unless you're really into fitness and in rather good shape). access: Feel free to walk around, the cabin is set on 5 acres, so there's plenty of space to clear your head, enjoy the night skies, and fresh air. Rathmichael is where city-folk come to bike, run, hike, forage & hill-walk their troubles away, so expect to encounter a fair number of outdoorsy-types once you leave our gates. There are fantastic walking, cycling and orienteering trails spread all over the area.  Moving on from our gates, hikers can enjoy both Barnaslingan Forest and the Carrickgollogan Forest Trail. Golfers meanwhile have a choice of either Old Conna Golf Club or Dun Laoghaire Golf Club, both of which are a short walk away. The Dargle River Valley is 15 minutes away by car, and Rathmichael Woods is a ten minute walk from the gate, if you fancy exploring a larger local woodland.  Essentially, the cabin is in the exact middle of a 5 acre market garden set on a hillside, and we aren't around much. We might turn up to check the gates, water the plants, or do a bit of work from time
interaction: The cabin is perfect for guests who want lots of open outdoor space and privacy -- that said, if you need us we're available by phone and we live a quick 15 minute drive away, in Killiney. You might see us working from time to time, but essentially, you'll be left to your own devices. The cabin does have a few neighbours, but they aren't going to hear you unless you're very loud, so you can feel free to sing, dance, and play your music. (We draw the line at Primal Scream Therapy or anything else that might prompt one of the local farmers to call emergency services. There are sometimes walkers up on Carrickgollogan (at the very top of the hill) which is a public park, after-all, and they might stare if you're doing anything really strange, so we do suggest you keep that in mind if you're hanging out near that back fence.
house_rules: The cabin is on a hillside, overlooking South County Dublin. You might encounter wild rabbits, foxes and deer, as well as nettles, ticks, muddy spots, slippery rocks, high things you could fall off of, and similar outdoor hazards. Please be in reasonably good physical shape, wear appropriate shoes, and have good common sense about things to do (and NOT do) in the countryside. The main gate must be kept closed at all times to ensure your privacy and security.
host_about: Our friends claim we're always hosting get-togethers, and we do really enjoy having guests, and yet, I think of myself as a private person. My partner and I have two sons (aged 9 & 13) so we spend a lot of our time parenting, as well as looking after the market garden. Before settling in Dublin I lived in New York, and although I've travelled through much of Europe and North America, I've yet to make it to Asia. (Japan features prominently on my to-do list, so please share your suggestions, if you have any). I'm a very independent traveller and while we like to meet new people and enjoy having visitors, we also tend to attract guests who value the farm for the creative freedom it offers. I was lucky enough to be chosen as a Fellow of the Edward Albee Foundation, so I've tried hard to recreate the vibe of a creative retreat. I hope you find our hillside farm as comfortable, cozy and inspiring as I do!

The latter part of the seventeenth and early eighteenth century was a period of considerable growth for the area. notes: Please make yourself at home! • It is advisable to book one night before your arrival if you require an early morning check-in to ensure early access. • The south inner city is the true city centre where all the best shopping, cultural activity and nightlife is. neighborhood_overview: The house is located in Stoneybatter. The neighbourhood has plenty of of old school Dublin character but has been known as an "up-and-coming" part of the city for quite some time now. It is precisely this mixture which makes Stoneybatter appealing to locals and tourists alike. Apart from the striking red brick artisan dwellings, the area is also known for the prominent Viking street names. For example, there is Viking Road, Olaf Road, Thor Place, Norseman Place, Ard Ri Road, Ostman Place & Sigurd Road. At the time of the Norman invasion, the Vikings, Ostmen or Austmenn (men of the East) as they called themselves, were exiled to the north of the Liffey where they founded the hamlet of Ostmenstown it what is now Stoneybatter. Stoneybatter has a great choice of places to eat and drink. Brunch and dinner spots include Cotto, Slice and Wuff. neighborhood_overview: Once you reach the end of our tranquil little alley you are transported as if by magic to a very different place, Lower Camden Street in the heart of Dublin's Portobello area. This area is full of local pubs, cool little cafes, an incredible array of international dining (from Vietnamese Street food to high end French restaurants), funky little shops, graffiti laden buildings and a variety of historic architecture and alleyways.
notes: Please note that while our little house and street is usually very tranquil during the day, there are some nightclubs on nearby Harcourt St toward the rear of the house as well as busy bars and restaurants on Camden St. As one might expect from an urban area this means there can be a little extra noise during the night, so we'd advise looking elsewhere if you are a light sleeper or easily bothered by noise. Also because we truly are a 'mini' house we really are small but beautiful. As a result space is at a premium and it is not suitable for guests with a lot of luggage.
transit: Only 5 minutes walk you will be in St Stephen's Green with its historic and relaxing gardens, the shops of Grafton Street and Dublin's Trinity College. 10-15 mins in a different direction will take you to the famous & historic Temple Bar area, Dublin Castle, the Guinness storehouse and a huge number of galleries and museums. Basically everything is on your doorstep here! You are a walk to pretty much everything but if you wish you also have multiple bus services right on the doorstep, the LUAS tram service, and easy connections to anywhere you might wish to travel.
access: Access to the whole house and garden apart from the host's room. Kitchen facilities may be available upon request but we recommend our guest's take advantage of one of the best areas for quality international food and drink in our neighbourhood of Portobello and Camden St
interaction: We are often working from home so you will probably see us here when you are home. We have both worked in the hospitality industry for a number of years so we're very experienced at making guests feel comfortable but also allowing them their own space. We also know Dublin well enough to be able to make some good recommendations for your time in the city. Note that Veasna is an award winning chef, specialising in South East Asian cuisine and we might even invite you to dine with us.

Irish girl with a genuine passion for hospitality and travel.

neighborhood_overview: Quintessential Georgian Dublin. Right out of story books and film, this is about as (posh) Dublin as you can get.  Temple Bar - famous for its wild and raucous nightlife - is about 15-20m walk away, so when booking please keep in this in mind, especially if you're looking to stumble out of a pub and into a flat. There are loads of iconic pubs, fun bars, and exciting nightlife to be found within a 5-10m walk from the flat, but this is not a hectic or rowdy area of Dublin.  There are embassies a few foot steps away, as well as stunning Merrion Square Park, the location of the world famous Oscar Wilde statue. Excellent restaurants and well-weathered pubs that have catered to everyone from iconic Irish writers, poets and politicians to friendly everyday folks are located within a few minutes walk.  The Natural History Museum and National Gallery of Ireland are a 3-5 minute walk away.  One block away at Merrion Square (and other nearby locations) you can catch buses all day long that will t
notes: The flat is well-equipped with everything from a hairdryer, umbrellas, clothes iron, to full kitchen with utensils and a brand new clothes washer.  ** Please note that the clothes washer does not have drying capability.  ** Wi-Fi IS NOT SET UP for the flat. My apologies, but I simply use unlimited cellular data (sim card) for my internet and laptop use using the 'Personal Hotspot' feature on my I-phone. You don't have to go to a cafe or library to find internet, I highly recommend checking out one of the many local cellular shops nearby. TheThree Store on Grafton Street (URL HIDDEN) has an extensive but inexpensive plan that allows unlimited data and text for the duration of most stays.
transit: Because the flat is situated just a couple minutes from the city center, you'll have options galore when it comes to transportation. Just about *everything* is within walking distance - Dublin is flat, so this helps!  One block away at Merrion Square (and other nearby locations) you can catch buses throughout the day and late night that take you all over the city as well as the airport. Airlink airport busses are a great option to get to and from the airport as they are inexpensive, quick and pick you up outside of Merrion Square Park just a few minutes walk away.  (URL HIDDEN) There are a handful of DART train stations nearby, the closest is either Grand Canal or Pearse Street. I prefer to take the DART from Grand Canal. Day trips to Bray, Killiney Hill/Dalkey, Malahide and Howth are highly recommended and simple to do on the DART.  (URL HIDDEN)

It was from this area that Georgian Dublin gained its roots and then spread throughout Dublin, something you'll easily spot in the local architecture. It may not have been as grand as the oppulent townhouses of the Southside but nearby you'll find there is a wealth of Georgian and Victorian architecture to see including Henrietta street, which is the earliest Georgian Street in Dublin and home to the Tenement Museum and Kings Inn. Other nearby attractions include Dublin's original reservoir - the basin, is just around the corner and its a lovely place to have a picnic and feed the ducks. Fairview Park is a short stroll and the Royal Canal Way is across the road. North Strand is also home to the award winning Mud Island Community Garden, which welcomes visitors. neighborhood_overview: Portobello is Dublin's famous Jewish Quarter. The neighbourhood was developed in the 1800's with beautiful tree lined streets and Victorian red brick houses.  It has buckets of charm and history - it's the birthplace of George Bernard Shaw and the neighbourhood picked by James Joyce as Leopold Bloom's home in Ulysses. In recent times Portobello has become an area known for its artistic community, great mix of cultures and a laid back vibe, with some of the city's best cafes, bars and restaurants (3 of which have been awarded the Bib Gourmand).  It’s the perfect place to stay to get a real experience of Dublin was recently voted the best place to live in Dublin by Lovin Dublin online magazine ! Dublin City centre is relatively small and for a short trip the best area to hang out runs for about 2km (1.5 miles) south from the River Liffey to the Grand canal. See map in photos.  Portobello is at the south (canal end) of that area and is perfectly situated to take on the best of the city.
notes: There are two double bedrooms and two bathrooms. The first bedroom has an ensuite bathroom off the bedroom. The second bedroom has a bathroom downstairs.
transit: Portobello is a beautiful old neighborhood that is best explored on foot and you can also walk to most of Dublin’s main tourist attractions, restaurants and bars.  Alternatively, you can take a Dublin City bike or jump on a tram or bus - all very close. There are multiple buses that service the city sites running from bus stops within a 2 min walk. Make sure to also explore the city along the canal which is quaint and beautiful, again just a 2 minute walk from the house.  There are lots of local cafes, bars and restaurants within a 5 minute walk. Camden st / South William St / George’s St / Grafton  St /Stephens Green, Main museums, National Gallery, Trinity College etc are all within a 1 to 2km walk or a short bus or tram journey. If you like, we can mail you lots of suggestions of where to go and what to do after you book.

name: Georgian gem wedged between Stoneybatter&the park
summary: Old Georgian house between Phoenix Park & Stoneybatter - Heuston Station and the Luas tram (Museum stop) are less than 5 mins walk away - we're just across the river from the Guinness factory. Fires in all bedrooms, new mattresses, wood-burning stove. New kitchen, new bathrooms and snugmaking central heating system. Refurbishment ongoing, so not all areas of the house are in use yet - we live here usually, and we love it as it is full of character, but it won't be for everyone!
space: The house is a listed building, built in the 1770s when Dublin was in its Georgian heyday. It was constructed on a grand scale, with 3.9m high ceilings, almost floor to ceiling windows in some rooms and beautiful pitch pine floorboards which have survived almost 250 years in remarkably good condition. The bus or tram will take you directly to the city centre but you may also cross the main road and take a woodland path up to Barnaculla, stopping for a pint at The Blue Light, before continuing on up to the great rocks at the summit of the Three Rock Mountain. There you can see a panoramic view of the city and Dublin Bay looking north and Dublin and Wicklow Mountains looking south. name: Massive room in an old Georgian house by the park
summary: Very large room (43m2) in old Georgian house between Phoenix Park & Stoneybatter - Heuston Station and the Luas tram (Museum stop) are less than 5 mins walk away. 1 double & 1 single bed with new mattresses. The room has central heating and a large open fireplace, as well as a dining table. You are also welcome to use the kitchen. The bathroom is not ensuite but is not shared. We are renovating gradually - we live here ourselves and love it as it is full of character, but won't be for everyone!
space: The house is a listed building, built in the 1770s when Dublin was in its Georgian heyday. It was constructed on a grand scale, with 3.9m high ceilings, almost floor to ceiling windows in some rooms and beautiful pitch pine floorboards which have survived almost 250 years in remarkably good condition. Many of the walls have been stripped back to reveal the early Georgian plaster and paintwork. name: Dublin City Centre-Georgian Home. Superb Location!
summary: Hi & welcome to our beautiful city centre home. We are located in the heart of the Docklands, a thriving new area and home to the majority of tech companies who have their EMEA HQs in Ireland.  Our square, Pearse Square, has been here since 1839, but most of the surrounding area was wasteland and derelict up until the quite recent development began in 2000. It now is an eclectic blend of old and new, with the vibrancy and energy of a booming tech scene mixed with salt-of-the-earth Dublin charm
space: We live on a Georgian Square, in a spacious three-story townhouse (1800 square feet). The top floor comprises of a double bedroom, a baby bedroom (with lots of toys to play with) and a room that we use for our personal storage.  On the middle floor, the floor you enter on, there is a double bedroom (with a super king mattress) and a living room. On the bottom floor, there is a kitchen, a dining room and a family bathroom. Pearse Square itself is a Georgian garden square bounded on its southern side by Pearse Street. This house was built in 1839. In the next year we will be doing it up as it needs a good and full renovation, however, we have been living here for more than a year with our toddler and it is very comfortable and warm. If you come with young children, there are a few things that you should be aware of which I've detailed in the section "Other things to note".

notes: Things you should know: As the house is old and pending a renovation, if you come with young children, they need to be watched all the time as there is a loose fire grate, loose pictures and heavy mirrors leaning against the wall and uneven surfaces on the basement level.  We manage with our toddler but she is used to the space and we would want you to be cautious. We also dont have a full kitchen. We have an induction hob (with one ring) and a small fridge, but there is no oven or microwave.  There is one bathroom with a large bath, shower and toilet and the house is very warm. There are other small imperfections in the house, like wood missing from the bottom of some of the architraves, some holes in walls and ceilings, loose skirting boards, exposed pipes - nothing crazy out of the ordinary and everything is safe, but some tired elements all the same that we will amend in our renovation project.  Hopefully you will love the charm of the house that these things are all a part of.
transit: The DART (Pearse Street DART station is under 10 minutes walk) as is Grand Canal DART station, beside (Hidden by Airbnb) HQ. You can also catch a boat from the River Liffey to some coastal towns North and South. Pearse Street is also one of the main bus corridors in the city so you can pick up most busses from there (check out the Dublin Bus website).
access: This is our home, and when you are here it is your home too - the whole house is accessible to you and your family.  (We keep a room at the top of the house that we use for our personal storage).
interaction: We travel overseas a lot and this is normally the reason we let out our home, however we will normally get family to let you in. During your stay (if we are not around), my mum will be on hand to help out with anything that you need.
house_rules: We have a young child so we don't wear shoes in the house. If you're comfortable doing the same, we have left a basket of slippers at the hall door. Complementing its food scene are its bars and nightlife, and within minutes of this quiet residential neighborhood, you will discover cosy traditional pubs and cool trendy bars. This is also the best spot to explore the city and its cultural and historic highlights, with the main sites and streets only a 10-15 minute walk from the property. Shop along iconic Grafton Street, rub shoulders with scholars at Trinity College, embrace the kitsch Irish scene of Temple Bar, taste the ‘Black Stuff’ at the Guinness Storehouse, gaze up at the beautiful architecture of St Patrick's and Christchurch cathedrals. There will be more instructions in the house and our own recommendations, but you couldn't be closer to such an excellent variety. The area is not exactly pristine gardens and white picket fences, but it's wonderfully diverse, young and full of life. There's a small park nearby, or else you're pretty close to one of Europe's largest city parks, Phoenix Park and a short walk from some of the pretty squares on the south side of the river.
notes: Capel street really has it all, including some of my favourite restaurants in the city. Start your day with coffee and a treat from Mish Mash, Outhouse, Brother Hubbard, or Camerino. From Asia you can get Dim Sum at Mr. Dinh, Pho at Aobaba, Sushi at Musashi, Korean Barbeque at Arisu, Schezuan at Old Town, or Malay at Kopitiam. If you can make it the full way down the street towards the quays without finding anything that tickles our fancy Klaw Poke does excellent seafood. For a snack on the go try the Brazilian offerings of Coxinha and Pao de Quiejo at Mercado Brasiliero. In the evening choose from The Beer House or the Black Sheep for your more hipster option or go to Slattery's and Pantibar, which have been around a little longer. That's all without leaving Capel Street!

Coming from the airpot you can get off at O'Connell street and walk from there, but if you're in a rush a taxi takes about 20 minutes and won't cost much more than that.

host_about: I'm a Dubliner who loves beautiful places, spaces, music, history, art and food. I adore local places with long histories and like to get to know them. My desert island foods would be crumbly blue cheese on an oat biscuit, butter and whiskey wrapped fresh lobster and Cork dry gin with slices of homegrown cucumber and ice. I can't live without good coffee and wouldn't even try. I'm currently reading Hal Fisher's A History of Europe and I love the knowledge it shares about Western Europe since 1731. Right now I'm catching up on my local history over the last 100 years...bound to happen in 2016 ... as the 100 years since the rising that sparked Ireland's independence comes calling.   My favourite musicians are plenty - Queen,  The Mumfords, Daft Punk and closer to home U2 and Mark Geary. I believe in keeping life simple - and I fundamentally believe - the simpler, the better. I enjoy welcoming guests to Dublin and sharing stories of local history, culture and food.

neighborhood_overview: Essentially the Naul is a rural village which still enjoys the friendly ambience of a previous time while also giving access to everything a modern city has to offer. The village is popular with recreational cyclists, who use the Seamus Ennis Centre with its cottage style and traditional thatched roof as a rest venue, especially at weekends. The centre also hosts music and other concerts and workshops with the focus being on traditional Irish and country/bluegrass music and dancing. A full list of the events will be available in the apartment. There is one pub, Killians, where you can enjoy meeting the locals near a real cozy fire. There is one church (RC) and only one shop in the village. But if you hanker after the bright lights then you are spoiled for choice with lots of restaurants, pubs, night clubs and big shopping centers all within twenty minutes drive away. You can take your pick from up to fifteen golf clubs, horse riding and many excellent beaches along the nearby east coas
notes: A car will give guests freedom to access local sporting and social attractions more easily but there is a Local Link bus service ( route 195 from Ashbourne and Balbriggan) visit Local Link.ie  or ph (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) and a local taxi service which can provide connections to larger towns and transport links to the whole country. If you enjoy things cultural then you might like to visit Ardgillen Castle and it’s 200 acres of parkland which was built in 1738 and is open to the public, or go really back in time and visit Fourknocks Passage Graves which is about 5,000 years old. Both of these are close by the Naul, and you can collect the key to the passage graves from the caretaker, who lives about a mile away, and spend as long as you wish exploring them. host_about:
Hi, I’m a family guy with a passion for world travel and new cultural experiences, be that from staying in other people’s homes, or other people staying in my home!

I’ve travelled all of the earth’s continents extensively, except for Antarctica that is, but it is on my bucket list :)  I’ve slept in AirBnB’s, mud-huts, tree-huts, slums, mansions, tents, deserts, churches, mountain cabins and boats to name a few! There is one thing I loved that was common to them all - meeting the people who live there and making new friends in this global village of ours.

I love to host people. My family’s home and dinner table is always open to guests and so I hope to have you join us soon!

host_about:
Married in 2013 Alice and Radek are a couple in their late thirties and parents to two little twins Max and Sofia. Radek is originally from the Czech Republic and is a potter who loves to work with porcelain. His pottery is Touch Design Ceramics check out- touchdesignceramics.  Alice Coghlan is a theatre and opera director with Irish/English/American heritage who runs her own company in Dublin Wonderland Productions - wonderlandtheatre, whose work includes literary audio walks of James Joyce's Dublin, children's theatre workshops and dinner theatre. She is also a qualified cook and loves to experiment with all the foods of the world and cook for our guests! 

In our spare time we love all things cultural and are very involved in the Dublin arts world and actually met by chance in a Dublin art gallery. We also enjoy hillwalking, movies, fine living, fun times and above all travel!

Between us we must have traveled 50 countries, and together have traveled from Prague to Istanbul together by train, from Gambia to Mali, all over Ireland and the Czech Republic, and for our recent honeymoon went around Italy with airbnb and enjoyed six wonderful stays with Italian families. So we know both what it is to host and to be a guest on airbnb!

We may also be able to offer you individual pottery or cookery classes with us during your stay, and you're also very welcome to visit Radek's pottery and to learn how pottery is made. 

We love being guests and hosts Airbnb so much that the the Irish Media got in contact with us, and one interview has led to another and we've been having a great time. Look us up 'listen again links' on radio shows RTE 1 Morning Ireland, Today FM Business Show on a Sunday or in newspapers Irish Independent and Daily Mail. The gorgeous pictures of us on our profile were taken by Stephen from the Irish Independent at our home.

The DART and LUAS (Dublin's light rail systems) also stop at Connolly station, and it is a short 15 minute train to Dublin's beaches and beautiful cliff walks. neighborhood_overview: Just North of the River Liffey and a short walk from historic O'Connell Street, this is the very heart of the city centre and the perfect location for anyone wishing to explore the city by foot. One of Dublin’s main shopping hubs is O'Connell Street (and its tributary, the ever-busy Henry Street), which culminates in a spearhead of excellent museums dotted around Parnell Square (most notably the Hugh Lane Gallery). To the west of here is the up-and-coming Smithfield and, further still, the vast Phoenix Park (also home to Dublin Zoo) while just across the bridge to the south is the formidable campus of Trinity College, with its ancient claim to fame in pride of place in the Old Library & Book of Kells. You have everything at your doorstep in the city centre and there's an exciting mix of cultures and ideas to cater for every whim you might have. host_about:
I would describe myself as honest, reliable, caring and understanding.

I love history and the classics, I studied them in university and have never lost that interest. Really like Irish history, the vikings and the ancient world.

I do a lot of voluntary work, it is a big part of who I am. I have been involved for over 20 years supporting different organisations and projects. I think life can be very hard for people and if you can help a little and bring a bit of light into a dark time, you should.

Am a dreamer, I love old buildings and castles. If I had a few million, I would restore old buildings/castles to their former glory. I think its sad to see an old building neglected and unloved especially ones of cultural importance.

I have a really bad memory for names, I mix up my boys. My father called my by his sisters name for most of my life, so I am totally blaming him on this fault in my character. 

My hosting style varies, I keep a clean house, your room is prepared and cleaned and I do your bathroom everyday. I normally try to work out, what sort of interaction a guest needs. Some guests just need a little support and are happy to stay private and relax in their room, others need/want more interaction. I base my style on what I pick up from my guest. 

My own private time, I watch films, read books or watch documentaries, I pop the laptop or book beside me and curl under the duvet, my little bit of heaven.

My married and have two boys 7 and 10, motherhood changes you in many ways, I love children and I love their imagination, their endless questions and desire for knowledge and often quirky way of looking at the world. There is never a day that goes by, that I don't laugh at some statement or comment from one of my children.

Our house is 60 years old, when we bought it, it was falling apart. Myself and my husband spent 2 years learning new skills or doing hard labour. We learnt loads of new skills, cried a lot and made great neighbours who did really help us. Not sure I would ever tackle that level of work again.  Don't mention the building work in ear shot of my husband or the old photographs will come out !!!!

host_about:
I would describe myself as honest, reliable, caring and understanding.

I love history and the classics, I studied them in university and have never lost that interest. Really like Irish history, the vikings and the ancient world.

I do a lot of voluntary work, it is a big part of who I am. I have been involved for over 20 years supporting different organisations and projects. I think life can be very hard for people and if you can help a little and bring a bit of light into a dark time, you should.

Am a dreamer, I love old buildings and castles. If I had a few million, I would restore old buildings/castles to their former glory. I think its sad to see an old building neglected and unloved especially ones of cultural importance.

I have a really bad memory for names, I mix up my boys. My father called my by his sisters name for most of my life, so I am totally blaming him on this fault in my character. 

My hosting style varies, I keep a clean house, your room is prepared and cleaned and I do your bathroom everyday. I normally try to work out, what sort of interaction a guest needs. Some guests just need a little support and are happy to stay private and relax in their room, others need/want more interaction. I base my style on what I pick up from my guest. 

My own private time, I watch films, read books or watch documentaries, I pop the laptop or book beside me and curl under the duvet, my little bit of heaven.

My married and have two boys 7 and 10, motherhood changes you in many ways, I love children and I love their imagination, their endless questions and desire for knowledge and often quirky way of looking at the world. There is never a day that goes by, that I don't laugh at some statement or comment from one of my children.

Our house is 60 years old, when we bought it, it was falling apart. Myself and my husband spent 2 years learning new skills or doing hard labour. We learnt loads of new skills, cried a lot and made great neighbours who did really help us. Not sure I would ever tackle that level of work again.  Don't mention the building work in ear shot of my husband or the old photographs will come out !!!!

neighborhood_overview: Ballsbridge is arguably Dublin's most exclusive address. Streets such as Shrewsbury Road and Ailesbury Road boast the highest real estate prices in Ireland with asking prices of up to €50 million for a single property. The area has traditionally been the home of the majority of foreign embassies and diplomatic representations in Dublin. It is not hard to see why the rich and powerful come to Ballsbridge: Originally developed in Victorian times, the streets are wide and tree lined and houses are substantial and set back in vast private grounds. Of all Dublin areas, Ballsbridge has the least built-up and most 'private' feel. Yet, despite the space and relative tranquility, Ballsbridge is only minutes away from the city centre.

host_about:
I would consider myself to be a citizen of the world and therefore feel that life for me is all about the experiences and memories that you treasure, those that you continually look back on and have pleasure in talking about.

To that end travelling has become a passion and fuels my desire to experience different cultures and societies, above all it allows me to meet different people and create those memories.

When visiting different Countries however comfort is everything to me so I love food (of course) but often get into trouble trying to experiment with unknown dishes but don't worry I always make up for that by enjoying local wines (funnily enough always white) and cocktails.

Where would the World be without cocktails or come to think about it "liquor of any type" if your willing to try anything just that once.

The endless amount of destinations to choose from and the history, architecture and culture open to us amazes me, I always find myself re-evaluating my lifestyle and personal choices once I've been away and continually feel grateful in terms of what I have and the possibilities available to any individual if she or he puts his / her mind to it. 

Love meeting new people especially if they have interesting life stories or are from different warps of life, they always appear to have a different or more open aspect on the world or it seems life in general.

Couldn't live without an iron, a smart phone, a credit card, a comfortable pair of shoes or more importantly my partner who will always be the love of my life and hopefully soon to be wife. 

Favorite destination impossible to choose from, to many I've seen and want to go back to and to many still left to see and already on my listof must dos.

Books give me, action, espionage or mob related, probably the same with movies, although, every now and again something that will bring a tear to my eye most recently being The Help or The Bucket List or a classic The Shawshank Redemption etc. 

In terms of being a host I try to provide guests with any and everything they might possibly need to make their stay more enjoyable and comfortable, the more information I can provide the better, always good to no what is available locally and where to go if you need something, from the closest and best restaurant to renting a vehicle at a competitive rate, the nearest Church or good watering hole. 

Dublin is one of the most amazing cities in the world as everything is so accessible, the mountains or a beach all a 20 minute drive away or easily available to you via public transport.

As a major European city you will find a constant and endless abundance of culture and entertainment available to you. I just hope you have enough time to experience it all and if not it will just give you an excuse to return.

Ringsend has also recently become home to many new businesses, providing many options when it comes to dining and entertainment. Hallo und willkommen! 

Im Januar 2018 habe ich meinen Lebensmittelpunkt von Düsseldorf nach Malahide verlegt und vermiete in meinem Haus Gästezimmer sowie das 2. Haus meiner Familie, das sich nur ein paar Haustüren entfernt befindet. 

Beruflich bin ich in Beratung & Training sowie in der öko-fairen Mode tätig.

Ich liebe Reisen und treffe sehr gerne neue Menschen aus anderen Ländern und Kulturen. In Malahide habe ich den Ort gefunden, an dem ich alt werden möchte. Die freundlichen Menschen, die abwechslungsreichen Landschaften, die vielen Sportmöglichkeiten, die gemütliche Pub-Kultur und die allgegenwärtige irische Live-Musik üben eine starke Anziehungskraft auf mich aus. 

Meine Gäste betreue ich persönlich und individuell. Auch gemeinsame Ausflüge sind nach Absprache möglich.

Ich freue mich auch auf Deinen/Ihren Besuch!

Kirsten

neighborhood_overview: Just North of the River Liffey and a short walk from historic O'Connell Street, this is the very heart of the city centre and the perfect location for anyone wishing to explore the city by foot. One of Dublin’s main shopping hubs is O'Connell Street (and its tributary, the ever-busy Henry Street), which culminates in a spearhead of excellent museums dotted around Parnell Square (most notably the Hugh Lane Gallery). To the west of here is the up-and-coming Smithfield and, further still, the vast Phoenix Park (also home to Dublin Zoo) while just across the bridge to the south is the formidable campus of Trinity College, with its ancient claim to fame in pride of place in the Old Library & Book of Kells. You have everything at your doorstep in the city centre and there's an exciting mix of cultures and ideas to cater for every whim you might have.  Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!
transit: Getting to and from the Airport couldn’t be easier. The 747 Airlink Express Bus runs direct from the Dublins central bus station (BusAras), or there is a closer stop on Arran Quay which is just a short walk from the apartment, and costs €14 return. Alternatively, you can take a 20-30 minutes taxi that will cost roughly €20-€30, depending on traffic.  If arriving by train, the apartment is located close to Heuston Station, so you will not be far from your front door! The LUAS (Dublin's light rail systems) also stop at Smithfield, a 5 minute walk from the property. Being so central, most of your journeys can be made by foot. If you would prefer using public transport, you will also have easy access to several bus routes on O’Connell street. Pick up a Leap card from a local newsagent or Connolly Station and you will be able to use all public transport across the city while you are here. The grounds of 15th-century Howth Castle have rhododendron gardens and a transport museum with local trams. The 19th-century Martello Tower houses a vintage radio museum. The medieval ruins of St. Mary’s Abbey lie nearby. A clifftop trail has sweeping sea views, indeed H.G. Wells once remarked that Howth had "the finest views west of Naples". neighborhood_overview: I moved to the Liberties for its vibrant urban mix. The area has it all, from hip cafes (try Legit on Meath Street, Two Pups on Frances Street, or the famous Fumbally) to Meath Street's no-frills street market. There are many pubs from the traditional, to contemporary (drop into The Beer Market for craft beer) and of course the Guinness Storehouse. There are shops for groceries etc on Thomas Street, and antiques (if you like) on Francis Street. You're less than 10 minutes' walk from the Liffey, 15 Minutes from the Irish Museum of Modern Art at Kilmainham - the whole of central Dublin is within walking distance.

neighborhood_overview: Just North of the River Liffey and a short walk from historic O'Connell Street, this is the very heart of the city centre and the perfect location for anyone wishing to explore the city by foot. One of Dublin’s main shopping hubs is O'Connell Street (and its tributary, the ever-busy Henry Street), which culminates in a spearhead of excellent museums dotted around Parnell Square (most notably the Hugh Lane Gallery). To the west of here is the up-and-coming Smithfield and, further still, the vast Phoenix Park (also home to Dublin Zoo) while just across the bridge to the south is the formidable campus of Trinity College, with its ancient claim to fame in pride of place in the Old Library & Book of Kells. You have everything at your doorstep in the city centre and there's an exciting mix of cultures and ideas to cater for every whim you might have.  Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!

Alternatively, you can take a 20-30 minutes taxi that will cost roughly €20-€30, depending on traffic. If you prefer public transport, take the 700 Aircoach from the airport to the Leopardstown stop; a return trip only costs €14. The property is only a short walk from this stop.  If arriving by train, the apartment is located close to Connolly Station, so you will not be far from your front door! The DART and LUAS (Dublin's light rail systems) also stop at Connolly station, and it is a short 15 minute train to Dublin's beaches and beautiful cliff walks.  Being so central, most of your journeys can be made by foot. If you would prefer using public transport, you will also have easy access to several bus routes on O’Connell street. neighborhood_overview: Dublin, Ireland I really love Dublin 8 - it's the perfect mix of all the weird and wonderful things the city has to offer. It's chilled, it's lively, it's often gritty and it's home to tons of art, design and music studios.  It's a lovely piece of old Dublin, the neighbourhood having been constructed in 1923 on a field that was once used for drying and hanging the textiles of the cotton industry, hence the name, The Tenters. In some ways it feels like it's far away from the city, it's so calm. There's a great mix of people living in the area, from artists and actors to the typical Dublin 'aul wans', and plenty of funky cafes and proper old Dublin pubs just a short walk away. Though it's not quite in the centre of the action, everything you could need is a few minutes away. neighborhood_overview: Just North of the River Liffey and a short walk from historic O'Connell Street, this is the very heart of the city centre and the perfect location for anyone wishing to explore the city by foot. One of Dublin’s main shopping hubs is O'Connell Street (and its tributary, the ever-busy Henry Street), which culminates in a spearhead of excellent museums dotted around Parnell Square (most notably the Hugh Lane Gallery). To the west of here is the up-and-coming Smithfield and, further still, the vast Phoenix Park (also home to Dublin Zoo) while just across the bridge to the south is the formidable campus of Trinity College, with its ancient claim to fame in pride of place in the Old Library & Book of Kells. You have everything at your doorstep in the city centre and there's an exciting mix of cultures and ideas to cater for every whim you might have.  Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!
transit: Getting to and from the Airport couldn’t be easier. The 747 Airlink Express Bus takes you to the Irish Rail Building North Wall Quay, and then the property is a 13 minute walk away. Alternatively, you can take a 20-30 minutes taxi that will cost roughly €20-€30, depending on traffic.  If arriving by train, the apartment is located close to Connolly Station, so you will not be far from your front door! The DART and LUAS (Dublin's light rail systems) also stop at Connolly station, and it is a short 15 minute train to Dublin's beaches and beautiful cliff walks.  Being so central, most of your journeys can be made by foot. If you would prefer using public transport, you will also have easy access to several bus routes on O’Connell street. Pick up a Leap card from a local newsagent or Connolly Station and you will be able to use all public transport across the city while you are here.

neighborhood_overview: Grand Canal dock is an area in Ringsend (Dublin 4) near Dublin city centre. It is an enclosed harbour between the River Liffey and the Grand Canal, surrounded by the Grand Canal Docks. It has its own railway station (also known as Barrow Street Station) and is an approx 10 minute walk to Trinity College, Dail Eireann, IFSC, Merrion Square, St Stephen's Green, Ballsbridge and the RDS. The Grand Canal Square is the centerpiece of the Grand Canal Dock area, designed by renowned architect, Martha Schwartz. Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!

If you’d prefer to walk into the centre, you can reach O’Connell Street in roughly 30 minutes.  Another great way to get around the city is cycling, a 3-day pass costing only €5, with bike stations throughout the city. The nearest bike stand to the property is Station no. 69 Grand Canal Dock. If you wish to pop out of the city, you can do day trips to other cities and towns in the West and South of Ireland such as Westport, Galway and Cork. There two main intercity train stations in Dublin are called Heuston and Connolly.

One of Drumcondras main sights is Croke Park, where Ireland's national games of Gaelic football and hurling can be seen. This is therefore an ideal spot if you're heading to Dublin for a show or sport!  Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!

If you prefer public transport, take the 700 Aircoach from the airport to the Lr. Drumcondra Road stop; a return trip only costs €14. The property is only a short walk from this stop.  Exploring Dublin couldn't be easier with Drumcondra station just a short walk away and easy access to several bus routes on Drumcondra Rd Lower. Pick up a Leap card from a local newsagent and you will be able to use all public transport across the city while you are here.  Another great way to get around the city is cycling, a 3-day pass costing only €5, with bike stations throughout the city.  If you wish to pop out of the city, you can do day trips to other cities and towns in the West and South of Ireland such as Westport, Galway and Cork. It is an enclosed harbour between the River Liffey and the Grand Canal, surrounded by the Grand Canal Docks. It has its own railway station (also known as Barrow Street Station) and is an approx 10 minute walk to Trinity College, Dail Eireann, IFSC, Merrion Square, St Stephen's Green, Ballsbridge and the RDS. With its posh airs and exclusive residences, Ballsbridge is the home to foreign embassies, several rugby clubs and the Royal Dublin Society with its annual horse show. Of all Dublin areas, Ballsbridge has the least built-up and most 'private' feel. Yet, despite the space and relative tranquility, Ballsbridge is only minutes away from the city centre. Close to the apartment you’ll find the Aviva Stadium and the RDS Arena. On Pembroke Road, Leeson Street or Morehampton Road, you will find plenty of eateries, coffee shops, groceries shops, bars and restaurants a short walk from the apartment. The nearest bike stand to the property is  Station no. 56 Mount Street Lower. If you wish to pop out of the city, you can do day trips to other cities and towns in the West and South of Ireland such as Westport, Galway and Cork. There two main intercity train stations in Dublin are called Heuston and Connolly.

host_about:
Hi, my name is Suely, a 31 years old journalist who loves chocolate and mocha. I am married with a wonderful guy named Anderson and we live in Dublin.
I was born in Italy, grew up in Brazil and now live in Ireland so I am a kind of world  citizen. 
My true passions are travelling and see different places and its history, meeting its culture and its people and reading about anything, just give me a book or a magazine and I'll be happy for at least a good 2 hours.
With my hubby I share the love for cinema, the sea, series (GOT anyone?), photography and food. Yes, we are truly food lovers and it's hard to beat good food to make us happy! Ah, and music of course, he plays guitar and I sing (it was how we met) so music is an important part of our lives.
Together we traveled to Italy, Greece, France, Malta and England and we didn't even started. Did I say that we love to travel? =)
I am really attached to my family in Brazil, especially my 2 years old niece Chiara and I miss them so much (and my dogs) and my dream it would be the world without frontiers and without such distance!

As guests we love to be in clean and bright spaces with some privacy. We are newly weds, you know? We love friendly and chatting people and love to share our experiences and get advice from the real people to really live like locals when travelling and get the most of where we're staying.

As hosts we try to treat everyone who comes into our home as we would like to be treated, with kindness and respect. If you love to chat you found your place, we can talk while having a coffee or tea (or a pint, why not?) but if you want some peace and quiet we will respect that and you can enjoy your stay in your silent space. Whoever you are we try to make sure you are comfortable and feel welcome and at ease. 

We are a young couple really easy-going and high-spirits who came to Ireland to try different things and a better life so we really try to live the best that Dublin has to offer. And we love it! Do you need any advice about the city? Feel free to ask, if we can we will help you to have the best experience ever here. 

We work very hard but we always have some time to hang out with our friends, walk or simply go out to see the wonderful city we live in and feel how lucky we are. 

Our motto is: "Don't worry about a thing 'cause every little thing is gonna be alright" and  also "Happiness is only real when shared" so either if you are staying with us or us staying with you, let's spread some good feelings and share some happiness into this world!!

neighborhood_overview: Just North of the River Liffey and a short walk from historic O'Connell Street, this is the very heart of the city centre and the perfect location for anyone wishing to explore the city by foot. One of Dublin’s main shopping hubs is O'Connell Street (and its tributary, the ever-busy Henry Street), which culminates in a spearhead of excellent museums dotted around Parnell Square (most notably the Hugh Lane Gallery). To the west of here is the up-and-coming Smithfield and, further still, the vast Phoenix Park (also home to Dublin Zoo) while just across the bridge to the south is the formidable campus of Trinity College, with its ancient claim to fame in pride of place in the Old Library & Book of Kells. You have everything at your doorstep in the city centre and there's an exciting mix of cultures and ideas to cater for every whim you might have. The 747 Airlink Express Bus runs direct from the Dublins central bus station (BusAras) which is just a short walk from the apartment, and costs €10 return. Alternatively, you can take a 20-30 minutes taxi that will cost roughly €20-€30, depending on traffic.  If arriving by train, the apartment is located close to Connolly Station, so you will not be far from your front door! The DART and LUAS (Dublin's light rail systems) also stop at Connolly station, and it is a short 15 minute train to Dublin's beaches and beautiful cliff walks.  Being so central, most of your journeys can be made by foot. If you would prefer using public transport, you will also have easy access to several bus routes on O’Connell street. Pick up a Leap card from a local newsagent or Connolly Station and you will be able to use all public transport across the city while you are here. Hi my name is Paul and I live just around the corner so always available to help when I can.  I work for one of the big American Software companies here in Dublin as my day job but my real passion is building a short term holiday letting business. I now have 3 apartments in the same building. Having travelled extensively in my Job and also personally I have stayed in a lot of very ordinary over priced hotels. My mission is to provide accommodation to my guests whether for business or leisure that offers a superior guest experience for less money. I take great pride in making sure my guests are happy and that they always have what they need when they stay with me. I believe in delivering the kind of experience to my guests that I would like to receive if I was staying with them. I have recently refurbished all my units to the highest possible standards. High quality bed linen and mattresses to ensure you get a good nights sleep. I have also invested in high speed WiFi, USB charging points and a work space/breakfast bar in each apartment so that you can work comfortably when you are required to do so.
I love to travel myself but with 3 young kids its hard to get away these days which is why I loving hearing stories of other travellers who end up staying with me..
I am a big fan of Rugby & I would highly recommend you try and catch our local team Leinster play during your stay.  Cheers Paul

The food around the city centre is pretty good also, depending on where you go, I can recommend hundreds of good places near my apartment. neighborhood_overview: Clontarf (Cluain Tarbh), Co. Dublin, is a seaside suburb on the Dublin - Howth road. It is one stop on the DART from the city centre, has a cosy village atmosphere and most roads lead down to the sea. Some of the best roads back on to St. Anne's Park, with its award-winning rose garden. In 550 A.D. a church was founded on Castle avenue by St. Comgall of Bangor; nothing is known of its history. Clontarf is the celebrated as the place of Brain Boru's great victory over Leinster and Norse Dublin, Good Friday, 1014 A.D., where St. Lawrence Road stands today. Clontarf was a fishing village and a popular seabathing resort for city people around the time when the Vernon family were the largest land-owners in Clontarf. Why not cross over to Bull island for a picnic, via the road bridge, or go for a swim on Dollymount strand?

The city center of Dublin is classed to be from Dorset St to the North to Golden Lane to the South and from Caple St to the West to Gardiner St to the East. In simple terms O’Connell St is Dublin’s Main St so when looking for central accommodation a good question to ask is how far of a walk is it to O’Connell St. We pride ourselves in the fact that all our apartments are in the city center so if the reason you come to Dublin is to be central then you’re in safe hands with us.

We love Dublin for its history, its architecture, its parks, its theatres, its museums, its galleries, its restaurant’s, the music, the pubs, cafes, nightlife and the list goes on but above all what makes Dublin great are the people. Time and time again we have returning guests who simple love to come to Dublin for the criac and if that’s something you want to do then it would be our pleasure to make it a reality :)
Hugs

If you wish to pop out of the city, you can do day trips to other cities and towns in the West and South of Ireland such as Westport, Galway and Cork. host_about:
Hi there, I'm Emma and together with my husband Nick, two sons and one dog we call this place our home.

I am a lighting and furniture designer/maker focusing on doing my little bit for the earth by using reclaimed materials.

My husband is a Clinical Psychologist and together, I design and we make whatever it is we need for our home.

We tend to focus on using sustainable materials, source good quality second hand furniture and through clever design and imagination, flip items on their head to best suit our needs as a family.

Our home is a reflection of what clever design and imagination can bring and we like to think that we can prolong the life of an item by giving it a bit of TLC.

We love colour and know that it has a positive effect on our mental health.

The colours that we have used throughout the house invoke warmth in winter and cool in summer.

She's an old girl, our house, turning 103 this year but boy has she still got it! Oodles of character and original features, she offers little nudges to keep you reminded of her age but by no means is she unsteady on her feet.  This girl is as sturdy as she comes.

She offers you lots to look at.  She's a trend setter for sure while offering you all the comforts of a modern home.  Kick back & watch some TV in the Gentleman's themed smoking room, or head upstairs to the main bedroom where you can kick back on the "Sofed" and become a Jedi and battle the dark lord that is Vader. Alternatively, if you fancy a cuppa & some reading material well, you won't be short of something to read in the kitchen as two walls are adorned with pages from Eagle Annuals dating from the 1960's & funnily enough, some of the the articles are relevant to this day!

If you are looking for a throwback to the 50's, kick back at our original Eddie Rockets Diner booth (p.s. to get the real diner feel, just order in from the Diner itself!).

Fancy a bit of bird watching, just head to the bathroom where you can fill the bath, relax and take in the view.

You will see that we are a bit Star Wars mad in this house but a little kind reminder that this is my husband's prized collection and it's ok to look, but please don't touch. Replacements will be pricey and if it's one of those rare ones, ouch!

We have books to read, games consoles to play, toys to delve into, a bath to relax in. Please, we aim to offer a home from home experience for you but we do ask, please respect it.  We have put a lot of time, love and effort into to making it our unique, personal home that we hope you will enjoy.

neighborhood_overview: Ballsbridge is on the south side of the city. It has been the urban retreat of choice for Dublin's wealthy citizens since the 19th century. With its posh airs and exclusive residences, Ballsbridge is the home to foreign embassies, several rugby clubs and the Royal Dublin Society with its annual horse show. Of all Dublin areas, Ballsbridge has the least built-up and most 'private' feel. Yet, despite the space and relative tranquility, Ballsbridge is only minutes away from the city centre. The Aviva Stadium, the RDS Arena, Herbert Park, and the Bord Gais Energy Theatre are all within walking distance from the house. On Pembroke Road, Leeson Street or Morehampton Road, you will find plenty of eateries, coffee shops, groceries shops, bars and restaurants a short walk from the apartment. Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!
transit: The easiest way to get to the property from the airport is by taxi. The journey will take approximately 30-40 minutes and depending on traffic the journey costs between €30 - €40. If you prefer public transport, take the 703 bus from the airport. The property is only a short walk from the stop.  From the apartment, you will have easy access to bus routes to city centre right at your doorstep.  The nearest station is Dublin City South, Northumberland Road.  Another great way to get around the city is cycling, a 3-day pass costing only €5, with bike stations throughout the city. The nearest bike stand to the property is  Station no. 19, Herbert Place. If you wish to pop out of the city, you can do day trips to other cities and towns in the West and South of Ireland such as Westport, Galway and Cork. There two main intercity train stations in Dublin are called Heuston and Connolly.

transit: For most of the last century, Smithfield was a grimy if beloved part of Dublin’s inner city. Back in the 1960s, it was run-down enough to stand in for Berlin’s Checkpoint Charlie in The Spy Who Came In From The Cold. (Richard Burton famously gave the local pubs great business.) But during the last boom, the square was extensively redeveloped with swanky apartments, ground floor retail, and grand plans for a new urban quarter. For years, many apartments and almost all the retail units stood empty. The horse fair, a feature of the area for centuries, was gradually pushed out after some public order incidents. neighborhood_overview: Santry is a fabulous part of the city of Dublin. It is a busy part of the north side of the city. The local pub, the Swiss Cottage, is infamous around the locality and is a historic drinking spot for many famous people because of the establishment's long history. The food there is basic but pretty good also. If you are not into traditional Irish food , there is a classic Irish take away beside the pub. They do a great battered sausage and chips. Santry Park is a huge park in the heart of Dublin, it is beautiful place to chill out, play football, have a few drinks and enjoy the amazing Irish weather that we don't have everyday.

neighborhood_overview: Just North of the River Liffey and a short walk from historic O'Connell Street, this is the very heart of the city centre and the perfect location for anyone wishing to explore the city by foot. One of Dublin’s main shopping hubs is O'Connell Street (and its tributary, the ever-busy Henry Street), which culminates in a spearhead of excellent museums dotted around Parnell Square (most notably the Hugh Lane Gallery). To the west of here is the up-and-coming Smithfield and, further still, the vast Phoenix Park (also home to Dublin Zoo) while just across the bridge to the south is the formidable campus of Trinity College, with its ancient claim to fame in pride of place in the Old Library & Book of Kells. You have everything at your doorstep in the city centre and there's an exciting mix of cultures and ideas to cater for every whim you might have.  Please take a look at the guidebook on my listing for recommended places to eat and drink in the area!
transit: Getting to and from the Airport couldn’t be easier. The 747 Airlink Express Bus runs direct from the Dublins central bus station (BusAras) which is just a short walk from the apartment, and costs €10 return. Alternatively, you can take a 20-30 minutes taxi that will cost roughly €20-€30, depending on traffic. If you prefer public transport, take the 700 Aircoach from the airport; a return trip only costs €14.  If arriving by train, the apartment is located close to Connolly Station, so you will not be far from your front door! The DART and LUAS (Dublin's light rail systems) also stop at Connolly station, and it is a short 15 minute train to Dublin's beaches and beautiful cliff walks.  Being so central, most of your journeys can be made by foot. If you would prefer using public transport, you will also have easy access to several bus routes on O’Connell street. Pick up a Leap card from a local newsagent or Connolly Station and you will be able to use all public transport across the city

A popular residential area which is buzzing with students and young professionals, Rathmines has an easygoing pace of life and the atmosphere of a town within the city. This central location is close to fantastic eateries and within walking distance to famous landmarks including The National concert hall and The Iveagh gardens.
